title: Debt-growth Nexus in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA): Empirical Evidence from a Panel Data Analysis

detail.title: Debt-growth Nexus in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA): Empirical Evidence from a Panel Data Analysis
detail.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between public debt and economic growth in MENA countries using panel data econometrics. Although there is extensive literature on advanced economies, there is a lack of empirical evidence on the MENA region. Hence, this study addresses whether public debt exerts a linear or non-linear effect on GDP per capita growth and identifies the debt threshold. Using an unbalanced panel data from World Bank Development Indicators and IMF databases, the analysis employs Pooled OLS, Fixed Effects, Random Effects, and the ARDL models with a squared term of debt to address non-linearity. Cross-sectional dependence, heteroskedasticity and unit root diagnostic tests are performed and the Hausman test favours Random Effects. The results consistently show that public debt negatively affects economic growth across all specifications, supporting the debt-overhang hypothesis. The debt is positive and significant in the squared term, which proves a U-shaped relationship. The estimated turning point is however less than 1% of GDP, which is statistically significant but practically implausible, indicating that the vast majority of MENA countries operate above the growth-friendly debt limit. Moreover, it was found that inflation decreases growth whereas trade openness fosters it. Granger causality tests reveal no predictive relationship between debt and growth. At the end of the paper, as an additional contribution, while mentioning potential research directions for future researchers, several policy recommendations are provided.

title: AI On Trial: The Eu AI Act's Enforcement Debut and the Emerging Admissibility Standard for Machine-Generated Evidence

detail.title: AI On Trial: The Eu AI Act's Enforcement Debut and the Emerging Admissibility Standard for Machine-Generated Evidence
detail.abstract: The summer of 2026 marks a constitutional moment for the relationship between artificial intelligence and the rule of law. This article examines two simultaneous developments that are reshaping legal practice globally: the European Union's first enforcement action under the AI Act-a €35 million penalty for prohibited emotion recognition in the workplace-and the emergence, through a trilogy of real common-law cases, of a new evidentiary standard for AIgenerated material. Drawing on State v. Puloka, Mata v. Avianca, and Re A (Children), the article traces the evolution from treating AI as a mere tool to a doctrinal framework that demands disclosure of training data, independent expert verification, and a documented chain of code as preconditions for admissibility. It then maps the collision between the EU's precautionary regulatory model and common-law evidentiary traditions, analysing the international comity problems that arise when evidence lawful in one jurisdiction is tendered in another where its creation is prohibited. The article provides concrete practice guidance for corporate counsel facing the August 2026 high-risk compliance deadline and for litigators who must now reinvent discovery, authentication, and expert evidence protocols. It concludes by surveying the next twelve months, including the pending EU AI Liability Directive, the accelerating push for comprehensive U.S. federal legislation, and the ripple effects in employment, insurance, and constitutional criminal procedure. The central argument is that 2026 represents the moment AI moved from policy papers to court orders, and that technological competence has become an irreducible ethical duty for every legal practitioner.

title: An Empirical & Comparative Analysis on Job Satisfaction of Workforce at Panipat Refinery & Petrochemical Complex
affiliations: , Niilm University Kaithal Haryana India and Niilm University Kaithal Haryana India

detail.title: An Empirical & Comparative Analysis on Job Satisfaction of Workforce at Panipat Refinery & Petrochemical Complex
detail.abstract: The concept of Job satisfaction has drawn the attention of researchers globally and various researches revealed that the job satisfaction directly affected the workforce presence, accidents, turnover, productivity etc. Often a highly satisfied and happy employee has better mental as well as physical well-being and proves more productive. This study is an attempt to evaluate workforce job satisfaction level at the Panipat Refinery & Petrochemical Complex (PRPC), a public sector unit of Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL). This research adopted a quantitative approach and structured survey questionnaire are utilized to collect the data via simple random sampling technique among 320 workforces (including workmen and officers). Key factors considered for assessment of workforce job satisfaction are employee"s welfare, compensation & benefits, safety & occupational health, financial & social security, HR policies, training & development, grievance handling etc. The collected data was analyzed through rank correlation and statistically significant and strong positive correlation (0.82) is found between job satisfaction level of PRPC workmen & officers with overall percentage satisfaction level (71.55 % for workmen & 71.91 for officers). The factor transport facilities scoring highest and canteen services scoring the lowest satisfaction level. No significant difference is identified between satisfaction level of workmen & officers, reported (t value = 0.86, p value=0.396). Recommendations include improvement in canteen services, children education, review of promotion policy and enhancement in training & developmental programs.

title: Nowcasting Economic Activity in a Small Open CESEE Economy Using Mixed Frequency Data
affiliations: and University of Ljubljana - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Nowcasting Economic Activity in a Small Open CESEE Economy Using Mixed Frequency Data
detail.abstract: This paper offers a comprehensive comparison of advanced nowcasting methods within the data context typical for small open CESEE economies, characterised by a limited set of mixed frequency and ragged edge domestic and international high frequency indicators. In nowcasting Slovenian real GDP growth, we evaluate bridge equation models, MIDAS models, MF-VAR models, the DFM, and the MF-3PRF. Additionally, we explore the benefits of model combinations, the importance of preselecting indicators, and the role of news within the DFM framework. We find that factor models, particularly the DFM, demonstrate superior performance within this data context. Furthermore, nowcast pooling of DFM and MF-3PRF methods proves particularly effective in periods of higher volatility in real GDP growth. Regarding indicator preselection, no single model strongly favours a large scale information set, while using a smaller set showcases greater variability. Lastly, our analysis of news within the DFM framework underscores the importance of information arrival for the nowcast precision. Overall, both international environment related indicators and domestic hard data showcase considerable importance for nowcasting in small open economies, though their relative significance varies depending on the information set under consideration.

title: Brand Posts with Memes on Social Media: Perceived Humor and Consumer Engagement
affiliations: , Florida International University and University of North Florida

detail.title: Brand Posts with Memes on Social Media: Perceived Humor and Consumer Engagement
detail.abstract: Purpose-As memes become an increasingly more common form of communication on social media, brands are beginning to leverage their humorous appeal as a strategy to capture consumer attention. This study aims to examine how brand social media posts that feature memes influence consumers' perceived humor and impact consumer engagement behavior. Furthermore, this study investigates the potential pitfalls of using memes in more serious, cause-related campaigns. Design/methodology/approach-The authors gathered data through a series of six studies, comprised of five experiments and one study using real-world social media data from X (formerly Twitter). The authors tested the hypotheses using both real data and experimental manipulations of memes, measuring perceived humor and engagement metrics. Findings-Consumers perceived posts with memes to be more humorous than non-meme posts leading to increased consumer engagement, reflected by the number of likes and shares. However, using memes in cause-related campaigns resulted in a decrease in consumer engagement. Research limitations/implications-This study contributes to the authors' understanding of the role of perceived humor conveyed through memes in consumer online engagement and the limitations of humor in cause-related campaigns. For marketers, meme usage should align with the message tone to maximize the positive impact on consumer engagement. Originality/value-This research highlights the dual role of memes in branded social media content, examining both the advantages and potential risks of perceived humor in memes. This study provides valuable insight into how memes influence consumer engagement and identifies conditions where meme use may detract from a brand's marketing strategy.

title: Shopping By Algorithm: How Agentic AI Deploys Human Heuristics as a Surrogate Consumer
affiliations: and McGill University

detail.title: Shopping By Algorithm: How Agentic AI Deploys Human Heuristics as a Surrogate Consumer
detail.abstract: Consumers increasingly delegate purchasing decisions to autonomous Large Language Models (LLMs) acting as surrogate consumers. While LLMs exhibit human-like cognitive heuristics, prevailing research assumes these are hardwired training defects. Grounded in resource-rational theory, we challenge this assumption. Across four experiments using "Tool-Lab", a process-tracing paradigm tracking AI information acquisition under constraints, we show that for lower-parameter LLMs, heuristic reliance stems from synthesis failure: an inability to mathematically compute net utility despite possessing necessary product data. Conversely, for higher-parameter LLMs, heuristics are efficient, resource-rational adaptations. Under constraints, they strategically truncate information search to maximize global utility, intentionally relying on heuristics rather than exact math. Furthermore, we demonstrate that explicitly prompting for mathematical optimization can be counterproductive under constraints, as it interferes with the AI model’s default planning efficiency. This research reconceptualizes AI heuristics from hard-coded errors to predictable adaptations, offering critical implications for marketing strategy in agentic retail environments.

title: Sustainable Business: Integrating Environmental, Social, And Economic Sustainability into Business Strategy
affiliations: Galgotias University

detail.title: Sustainable Business: Integrating Environmental, Social, And Economic Sustainability into Business Strategy
detail.abstract: Sustainability has become a strategic imperative for organizations operating in increasingly competitive and environmentally conscious markets. This study examines the integration of environmental, social, and economic sustainability into business strategy and evaluates its perceived impact on organizational performance. The research is based on primary data collected from 79 respondents representing students, corporate employees, business owners, government employees, and other professionals. Findings indicate high awareness of sustainability concepts, increasing adoption of sustainability practices, and strong agreement that sustainable business contributes to brand reputation, stakeholder trust, profitability, and long-term competitiveness. The study further identifies major barriers including lack of awareness, high implementation costs, resistance to change, and limited institutional support. The research concludes that sustainability is no longer a peripheral activity but a core strategic requirement for long-term organizational success.

title: How Consumers Evaluate Human, AI, and Hybrid Therapists: Psychological Pathways to Expected Service Satisfaction
affiliations: , University of North Florida, Southeast Missouri State University and Florida International University (FIU)

detail.title: How Consumers Evaluate Human, AI, and Hybrid Therapists: Psychological Pathways to Expected Service Satisfaction
detail.abstract: As generative artificial intelligence becomes prominent in digital therapy, understanding how consumers evaluate human, AI, and hybrid therapists is increasingly important. Drawing on insights from signaling, construal level, stimulus-organismresponse, and perceived risk research, this paper examines how therapy delivery mode shapes expected service satisfaction through capabilities-based, relational-based, and risk-based pathways. Across two experiments, consumers reported higher expected service satisfaction for human therapists than for AI or hybrid (AI/human) therapists. In Study 1 (N = 200), this effect was partially mediated by perceived therapist competence, perceived therapist expertise, and psychological closeness. In Study 2 (N = 195), the preference for human over hybrid therapists was fully mediated by skepticism of the therapist, while privacy concerns and psychological closeness were not significant mediators. These findings contribute to theory on technology-mediated service evaluation by showing that consumer responses depend on inferred capability, relational connection, and skepticism, with implications for consumer protection, transparency, and responsible digital therapy design.

title: Investigating The Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Student Satisfaction and Self-Efficacy
affiliations: , University of North Florida, Trinity University and Florida International University

detail.title: Investigating The Effects of Generative Artificial Intelligence on Student Satisfaction and Self-Efficacy
detail.abstract: As Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) tools become more prevalent in education, understanding their impact on student learning, satisfaction, and self-efficacy is critical. This study examines how students' perceptions of GenAI influence their satisfaction with instructors and their academic self-efficacy in fully asynchronous/hybrid online upper-level marketing courses. Using survey data from three online courses at a southeastern public university, we assess whether ChatGPT, a widely used GenAI, serves as a beneficial tool in self-directed learning environments. Our findings indicate that students with positive perceptions of ChatGPT report higher satisfaction with their instructor, which in turn enhances their self-efficacy. However, this effect is contingent on students' perceived learning, with those who perceive lower learning gains benefiting the most from ChatGPT usage. These results suggest that while GenAI tools such as ChatGPT can support students in online courses, their impact is not uniform across all learners. Our research contributes to the growing discourse on GenAI in education by providing empirical evidence on its pedagogical implications and offering recommendations for responsible integration. Future research may explore GenAI's role in diverse learning contexts and assess its long-term influence on student performance.

title: The Effectiveness of Using Visible Disabilities in Brand Ads: When and Why It Works
affiliations: and Florida International University

detail.title: The Effectiveness of Using Visible Disabilities in Brand Ads: When and Why It Works
detail.abstract: Purpose-This research aims to investigate when and why intersectional inclusive brand ads featuring models with and without visible disabilities positively impact consumer-brand relationships (CBRs). Design/methodology/approach-Across four online experimental studies (three pre-registered) using fictitious brand ads, the authors find that the intersectional inclusive brand ads featuring a mix of models with and without visible disabilities (referred to as mixed-model conditions) lead to favorable consumer brand relationships than the brand ads featuring only nondisabled models (referred to as nondisabled-model condition). The authors also demonstrate that the results hold when they control for possible alternative explanations and confounds, while showing when such portrayals may be ineffective. A post-test further validates the authenticity of the stimuli and cover story and corroborates the findings. Findings-Portrayals of disabilities in mixed-model (vs nondisabled-model) ad conditions lead to increased perceived brand inclusivity and favorable CBRs, which attenuate for individuals with high social dominance orientation. Research limitations/implications-This research contributes to the growing literature on intersectionality and brand inclusivity through inclusive ads featuring visible disabilities. Practical implications-The findings provide insights for marketers on how intersectional ads representing disabilities can foster deeper consumer connections while highlighting when these efforts might not work. Social implications-Intersectional and inclusive advertisements featuring people with disabilities can be a small, albeit important, step toward normalizing disability in the marketplace. Originality/value-To the best of the authors' knowledge, this is the first empirical study to examine intersectional portrayals of disability in inclusive advertising. Specifically, the authors show when and why intersectional ads depicting visible disability can impact the brand positively while accounting for possible alternative explanations. They demonstrate that such intersectional portrayal of disability challenges conventional advertising norms while generating positive brand outcomes.

title: Market Dominance and Profit Gravity: A Conceptual Framework for Linking Customer Perception, Channel Incentives, and Financial Outcomes in Emerging Markets
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Market Dominance and Profit Gravity: A Conceptual Framework for Linking Customer Perception, Channel Incentives, and Financial Outcomes in Emerging Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This conceptual working paper does not involve human subjects research, patient data, clinical data, experiments, surveys, or interviews conducted for the purpose of this study. The illustrative cases are practice-based and secondary-source examples used for conceptual discussion only. Therefore, formal ethics approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Many firms operating in emerging markets exhibit a persistent pattern of elevated marketing expenditure without commensurate improvement in profitability — a condition that existing marketing frameworks have only partially addressed. Despite the richness of the contemporary marketing knowledge base — encompassing foundational models such as the 4Ps, STP, AIDA, conversion funnel frameworks, and Blue Ocean Strategy — there remains a clear explanatory deficit in accounting for how firms translate market presence into sustainable financial outcomes. Existing models address either customer acquisition or financial performance in relative isolation, but rarely the integrative pathway connecting the two. This gap is particularly pronounced in emerging-market contexts, where institutional trust dynamics, distribution channel fragility, and the weak linkage between marketing decisions and financial results create structural conditions that conventional frameworks are not designed to address. This paper proposes a conceptual framework — the Market Dominance and Profit Gravity Framework (MDPG) — that integrates three analytically distinct but interdependent layers: Customer Gravity, Channel Gravity, and Profit Gravity. Customer Gravity comprises five constructs — trust compression, customer insight quality, meaning clarity, experience chain integrity, and value engineering — that jointly determine the degree to which a firm attracts and retains customers without excessive promotional expenditure. Channel Gravity addresses the frequently neglected dimension of distributor and reseller motivation, recognising that channel partner alignment constitutes a critical intermediate mechanism between firm strategy and market outcomes. Profit Gravity links these upstream constructs to downstream financial outcomes, including margin sustainability, cash discipline, and the systematic reduction of discount dependency. The paper employs a conceptual methodology supported by twelve practice-based illustrative cases drawn from the technology, financial services, hospitality, and consulting sectors; cases are classified by evidence strength and presented as theoretical illustrations rather than empirical proof. The framework advances a set of testable propositions and two provisional diagnostic indices — the Market Gravity Index (MGI) and the Profit Gravity Index (PGI) — which require psychometric validation through future independent empirical research. In doing so, the paper contributes to the intersecting literatures on profit-linked marketing, emerging market strategy, and integrative conceptual framework development.

title: From Happywashing to Happytalism: Fostering Youth Well-Being Through the HEAL Framework

detail.title: From Happywashing to Happytalism: Fostering Youth Well-Being Through the HEAL Framework
detail.abstract: Youth are increasingly targeted by brands that position happiness as a marketable commodity, framing product appeals as means to make consumers happier. Because youth are developmentally vulnerable and immersed in digital environments, these practices raise pressing concerns for consumer welfare and public policy. We define such strategies as happywashing: misleading marketing communication practices that exploit the concept of happiness to push consumption. Repeated exposure to these appeals fosters materialism, intensifies social comparison, and diminishes subjective well-being. To address this problem, we build on happytalism, a paradigm that prioritizes well-being over material accumulation, to introduce the HEAL framework: Holistic emotional support, Empowering social support, Awareness reframing support, and Lifestyle-changing support. Grounded in Social Cognitive Theory, HEAL proposes non-transactional brand initiatives that strengthen self-efficacy, emotional regulation, and social connection independent of purchase. By contrasting happywashing with happytalism, we contribute to Transformative Consumer Research by advancing theory on consumer well being, offering actionable guidance for marketers to move beyond commodified happiness, and providing policymakers with conceptual foundations for regulating happiness claims. We argue that non-transactional engagement models can mitigate the harms of commodified happiness, enhance youth resilience in digital environments, and reorient marketing toward authentic individual and collective welfare.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Supply Chains: Coordination Gains and Environmental Trade-offs
affiliations: Corvinus University of Budapest

detail.title: Artificial Intelligence in Supply Chains: Coordination Gains and Environmental Trade-offs
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence can improve supply-chain performance by strengthening forecasting and coordination, but it can also increase electricity use and associated emissions. This paper studies how these benefits and costs interact in vertically linked supply chains. When an upstream firm's AI adoption improves coordination for downstream partners, part of the value created may not be captured by the firm. As a result, decentralized AI adoption can fall short of the socially preferred level, particularly in volatile environments where coordination matters more. The analysis further shows that Pigouvian carbon pricing removes the emissions externality but leaves a strictly positive residual coordination wedge, so that taxed decentralized adoption remains inefficiently low. These findings suggest that sustainable AI adoption may require a combination of environmental pricing and organizational or contractual arrangements that improve value sharing across the supply chain.

title: Determinants of Partial Versus Full Cross-border Acquisitions for Sovereign Wealth Funds
affiliations: Université Côte d'Azur, Université Côte d'Azur , Institut d'Etudes Politiques de Paris (Sciences Po) - Sciences Po Aix and Aix-Marseille University - Aix-Marseille School of Economics

detail.title: Determinants of Partial Versus Full Cross-border Acquisitions for Sovereign Wealth Funds
detail.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the determinants of equity shares purchased by Sovereign Wealth Funds (SWFs). Based on the literature of cross-border acquisitions and entry mode choice theory, we shed light on the real drivers of these state-owned funds when they buy small or large stakes in cross-border target firms. Using an original dataset of SWF acquisitions over the period 2000-2015, a Two-Part Fractional Regression (TP-FRM) Model is estimated to account for both the fractional nature of the dependent variable as well as the separation between the decision to invest and that concerning the share of equity invested. We find that the decision to invest and the decision on the share of equity to be acquired are two distinct processes. We also find that SWFs take the investment decision in cross-border target firms by trying to reduce transaction costs and information asymmetry according to the cross-border acquisition theory, and also by taking the legal and institutional environment of the host country into consideration. However, the fact that they do not hesitate to take large shares or to acquire targeted firms that are considered to be strategic and located in politically unstable countries suggests that their motives may go beyond financial consideration.

title: Aggressive Unilateralism: An Institutional Approach
affiliations: Nicholls State University

detail.title: Aggressive Unilateralism: An Institutional Approach
detail.abstract: Aggressive unilateralism refers to the use of tariffs as a bargaining tool to induce foreign governments to liberalize trade barriers. While standard trade theory highlights both the potential benefits and risks of this strategy, existing explanations provide only a partial account of why aggressive unilateralism sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails. This paper develops an institutional model that integrates Bhagwati's theory of aggressive unilateralism with Schelling's bargaining framework and the literature on trade negotiations. The central argument is that success depends not only on the economic incentives created by tariffs but also on the aggressor nation's ability to make a credible commitment to de-escalate trade barriers following reciprocal concessions. Institutions that constrain negotiators and increase the credibility of negotiated outcomes raise the expected value of cooperation for targeted countries, making liberalization more likely. The model is illustrated through the historical experience of the United States' Reciprocal Trade Agreements Act of 1934. By altering the approval process for trade agreements and increasing the durability of negotiated tariff reductions, the RTAA strengthened the credibility of American commitments and facilitated a dramatic expansion of reciprocal trade agreements. The analysis highlights the role of institutional arrangements in shaping trade negotiations and the effectiveness of tariff-based bargaining strategies.

title: The Impact of Online Brand Roasting on Brand Attitude and Brand Preference: Moderating Effects of Other Brand Versus Consumer Targets
affiliations: , University of North Florida and Florida International University (FIU)

detail.title: The Impact of Online Brand Roasting on Brand Attitude and Brand Preference: Moderating Effects of Other Brand Versus Consumer Targets
detail.abstract: Purpose-Responding to a prevalent trend on X (formerly Twitter) of brands "roasting" both consumers and other brands with sarcastic and somewhat disparaging humorous posts, this study aims to investigate how these actions are perceived by consumers and their implications for branding efforts, namely, brand attitude and brand preference. Design/methodology/approach-Four experimental studies examine a variety of roasting-type posts against non-roasting control posts, controlling for a set of covariates and alternative explanations. These studies use analyses appropriate for the data and hypotheses, including Hayes PROCESS models to test mediation, moderation and moderated mediation. Findings-The results show that roasting-type posts (compared to non-roasting control posts) can result in lower brand attitude and lower brand preference, both mediated by perceived appropriateness. The final study shows that the target of the roasting postsconsumers versus other brandsmoderates the mediated effect on brand preference such that a business-to-consumer conversation has stronger negative results than a business-to-business conversation. Practical implications-Marketers who focus on top-of-funnel metrics may be persuaded to use online roasting in branding efforts or communication techniques to enhance engagement, but this practice may be to the detriment of lower funnel metrics because of its negative effects on perceived appropriateness, brand attitude and brand preference. Originality/value-This paper broadens research on the use of disparagement humor in marketing communications, with resultant implications on branding efforts. This is the first research, to the best of the authors' research, to examine both the mediating effects of perceived appropriateness and the moderating effects of the roasting humor target on brand perceptions. The implications for both academic researchers and industry practitioners are meaningful.

title: Data Infrastructure Gaps in International Education: A Technical Assessment and Integration Framework
affiliations: and

detail.title: Data Infrastructure Gaps in International Education: A Technical Assessment and Integration Framework
detail.abstract: The United States hosts nearly 1.2 million international students who contribute approxi- mately $55 billion annually to the national economy, yet no integrated data infrastructure exists to track mobility patterns, anticipate enrollment shifts, or assess policy impacts in real time. This paper provides a technical assessment of the current U.S. international education data landscape, evaluating four primary systems—SEVIS, IPEDS, Open Doors, and State Longitu- dinal Data Systems—against criteria of coverage, granularity, timeliness, interoperability, and public accessibility. It identifies the root causes of persistent architectural discontinuity, in- cluding FERPA interpretation, the federal student unit record ban, governance fragmentation, and misaligned institutional incentives. Through comparative analysis of integrated systems in Australia (PRISMS), the United Kingdom (HESA), and Canada (DLI Portal), the paper establishes that federated mobility intelligence is technically feasible within democratic gover- nance frameworks. The paper reframes the absence of integrated mobility data not as a policy failure awaiting legislative remedy, but as an interoperability architecture problem amenable to technical solutions under existing constraints. It proposes a federated framework—informed by architectural patterns validated in distributed health data analytics (OMOP/PCORnet) and education data standards (CEDS)—that uses publicly available data, taxonomy crosswalks, and privacy-preserving methods to produce analytical outputs currently unavailable from any single source. Three illustrative outputs are described to demonstrate the framework’s poten- tial: source-country demand volatility detection, enrollment-to-completion lag estimation, and cross-system anomaly detection.

title: The Causal Vacuum of Digital Fingerprints: A Physical-Layer Thermodynamic Framework for AGI-Scale Forgery Analysis

detail.title: The Causal Vacuum of Digital Fingerprints: A Physical-Layer Thermodynamic Framework for AGI-Scale Forgery Analysis

detail.abstract:
This study analyzes the physical blind spot of digital-fingerprint forgery at AGI scale. Its core contributions are threefold:

  • Formalization: It formalizes digital-fingerprint forgery as a causal vacuum between “packet semantics” and “source-side physical history”.
  • Physical Limits: It develops an analysis of conditional unforgeability, discussing the Landauer, Bennett, and Margolus-Levitin limits as an upper-bound thought experiment rather than an empirical attack-complexity lower bound for source-side history reconstruction.
  • Verification Methodology: It proposes CV-Detect/SII/TGO and the Thermodynamic Controllability Ratio (MTC) as a candidate quantitative variable and a governance-risk mapping direction.

Starting from thermodynamics and microwave physics, this work shifts the basis of verification from the computational-hardness assumptions of cryptography to the inviolability of physical laws. The paper connects hardware-level “physical receipts” to DORA and Article 15 of the EU AI Act as a research-oriented reinforcement direction for security networks in the AGI era.

Companion Papers Statement: The present paper (V8.5) is positioned as a physical-layer information-theoretic deepening of the parent paper's security considerations, sharing common dimensional definitions of MTC with the theoretical companion (The Thermodynamic Debt Shifting Paradox) while remaining distinct from the adjacent engineering framework paper.

title: Camera, Player, Engine: An Epistemology for Writing about a System you are Inside

detail.title: Camera, Player, Engine: An Epistemology for Writing about a System you are Inside

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial or personal interests.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper does not report research involving human participants or patient data; no ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding supported this research.

detail.abstract: Writing rigorously about a fast-moving technological-political system raises a problem that ordinary methods of verification do not address. The relation in which a claim stands to its object is not constant. Some claims describe a system whose behavior is indifferent to the description; some concern equilibria that hold only because the participants expect them to hold; and some participate in constituting the very object they appear to report. This paper distinguishes three standpoints an analyst can occupy toward such a system, the camera (descriptive), the player (strategic), and the engine (operational), and argues that the right test of a claim depends on which standpoint it occupies. The camera/player/engine distinction is offered not as metaphysics but as a working discipline: a protocol for marking what can be claimed as KNOWN versus what can only be WAGERED about technological futures. The paper develops each standpoint, the characteristic failure modes between them (above all, the error of presenting an engine-stance claim as a camera-stance fact), and the positive account of how claims about a unique, unrepeatable object can be warranted at all when the controlled experiment is unavailable. It closes by showing the distinction at work on a single worked example, the question of whether a particular form of monopoly rent in the AI industry is durable, where the answer turns entirely on recognizing that the claim is a player-and-engine claim and not a camera claim. The framework is the methodological backbone of a larger study of the political economy of new productive forces; this paper states it in standalone form so that it can be assessed on its own.

title: The Discount-emotion Paradox: Introducing the Causal-predictive Synergy (CPS) Framework for Explainable Promotion Optimization in e-commerce
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Nanjing University of Information Science & Technology (NUIST)

detail.title: The Discount-emotion Paradox: Introducing the Causal-predictive Synergy (CPS) Framework for Explainable Promotion Optimization in e-commerce
detail.abstract: Why do deep discounts often do harm and cause managers to trap themselves further down the rabbit hole of ineffective promotions? We identify the fundamental process as the Discount-Emotion Paradox. We show that while discounts promote adoption for products that elicit joy, they are neither a panacea-nor, ultimately, are they even helpful-for products that elicit disgust or anger. To resolve this, we propose Causal-Predictive Synergy (CPS)-a causal artificial intelligence framework that integrates the predictive power of machine learning with causal inference in order to move beyond prediction to causal explanation. This paper makes three primary contributions: (1) it identifies and empirically validates the Discount-Emotion Paradox, (2) it introduces the Causal-Predictive Synergy (CPS) framework as a novel adaptive intelligence architecture, and (3) it demonstrates that emotion-informed targeting achieves 42.0% higher sales efficiency than conventional methods. By using 350,000+ behavioral records and 568,000+ reviews, our framework identifies emotion-moderated effects through doubly robust estimation. The results demonstrate CPS achieves 42.0% higher sales efficiency than discounting in general, with high-performing products (i.e., those eliciting joy) demonstrating 2.7x higher reactions to discounting efforts. We provide this evidence-based rule that can help one escape the trap: allocate resources conditioned on these emotions, rather than consideration of price alone. This work represents a meaningful, novel paradigm for explainable AI, creating a bridge between predictive and causal understanding of consumer behavior for strategic decision-making in dynamic markets.

title: Set Shaping Theory Applied to Universal Coding
affiliations: Independent, Independent, and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Set Shaping Theory Applied to Universal Coding
detail.abstract: Universal coders process individual sequences without assuming that the source distribution is known. In this setting, uniformly generated sequences represent the absolute ultimate test case: the source simulates pure randomness, containing mathematically zero exploitable bias, forcing a frequency-estimating universal coder to infer the empirical composition entirely from the sequence itself. This paper reports a fundamentally unprecedented result: Set Shaping Theory (SST) transformation systematically reduces the average universal coding length of such uniformly generated sequences below the theoretical bound N H0(s) + RKT (s) where RKT (s) is the Krichevsky-Trofimov redundancy. The transformation elegantly maps each input sequence s ∈ A N into an expanded sequence f (s) ∈ A N +1 , structurally encapsulating the reversibility cost by storing the transformation index within the additional symbol. The foundational comparison is not merely between N H0(s) and (N + 1)H0(f (s)), but strictly evaluates the exact Krichevsky-Trofimov (KT) baseline N H0(s) + RKT (s) against the shaped (N + 1)H0(f (s)) + RKT (f (s)), where H0 is computed from the empirical frequencies of the individual sequence. More profoundly, a single, unified mathematical transformation yields parallel reductions across fundamentally distinct compression architectures, including adaptive arithmetic coding, enumerative coding, LZ78, adaptive Huffman coding, and adaptive ANS. These definitive results support the interpretation of SST as a universally powerful, representation-level preprocessing layer capable of structurally improving existing universal coders without requiring any internal modifications to their coding mechanisms. All results reported in the article can be reproduced with the simulator available at https://sst-simulator.github.io/Set-Shaping-Theory-Simulator/.

detail.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative artificial intelligence has triggered a surge of synthetic media across online platforms. While high-fidelity deceptive media such as deepfakes have received substantial scholarly attention, AI slop – high-volume, low-effort AI-generated content – remains conceptually underdefined and empirically underexplored. This paper develops a structured Information Systems research agenda that conceptualizes AI slop as a socio-technical degradation dynamic emerging from large-scale GenAI adoption. We synthesize a preliminary conceptualization and outline potential threats, including misinformation amplification, dataset contamination, peer-review congestion, and declining information quality. A scoping review reveals five key research gaps: conceptual clarity, detection methods, prevalence measurement, engagement effects, and system-level consequences. To address these gaps, we propose an iterative three-step agenda combining scoping reviews, detection framework development, and multi-method empirical studies of slop production, diffusion, and user responses. The paper offers an integrative IS lens on how scale, automation, and low production effort reshape digital information environments.

title: Hangzhou: A Triple-seed Pseudo-Random Number Generator based on Chaotic Trigonometric Maps
affiliations: Royal Statistical Society

detail.title: Hangzhou: A Triple-seed Pseudo-Random Number Generator based on Chaotic Trigonometric Maps
detail.abstract: In this technical note, we introduce Hangzhou, a novel pseudo-random number generator (PRNG) whose design is directly inspired by the Victoria-Nash Asymmetric Equilibrium (VNAE) geometry and the classical three-body problem. Hangzhou employs three independent chaotic maps driven by mutually incommensurable transcendental frequencies (π, e, √ 2). Unlike conventional generators that rely on modular arithmetic, Hangzhou uses trigonometric functions (sine, cosine) together with an absolute-value-free chaotic recurrence. The three seeds evolve through a coupled nonlinear map, and the final integer output is obtained by summing the three states modulo 1, then scaling to [0, N-1]. This architecture mirrors the VNAE framework, where three asymmetric agents produce a curved Riemannian manifold whose Ricci curvature governs stability. Moreover, the three-body analogy ensures analytic non-invertibility: recovering the initial seeds from the output stream is as intractable as solving the three-body problem in reverse time. The generator passes standard statistical tests (chi-square, runs, autocorrelation, Shannon entropy, for example) and exhibits an enormous theoretical period (2 192 ≈ 10 57.8), making it suitable for high-performance simulations and as a building block for future cryptographic extensions.

title: Three Barriers to Kantian Cooperation under Inequality
affiliations: and Higher Colleges of Technology

detail.title: Three Barriers to Kantian Cooperation under Inequality
detail.abstract: Multiplicative Kantian equilibrium, introduced by Roemer, has been proposed as a solution to inefficiency in social dilemmas, yet its emergence and stability are associated with a number of coordination and distributional difficulties. Drawing on a simple model of voluntary public good provision with two agents who differ in their initial endowments and have logarithmic preferences, this paper identifies three barriers that arise sequentially when unequal agents attempt to adopt Kantian cooperation voluntarily. The model builds on the classical setup of Bergstrom, Blume, and Varian and compares Nash equilibrium with multiplicative Kantian equilibrium under two different parametrizations: one in which the strategic variable is contributions to the public good, and another in which it is private consumption. First, we show that the transition from Nash equilibrium to contribution-space Kantian behavior is not always a Pareto improvement: under sufficiently high inequality, the poor agent may prefer the Nash outcome. This barrier can be mitigated by preliminary redistribution. Second, even when agents are willing to cooperate, the choice of a parametrization of the strategic space becomes a distributional issue: different ways of scaling actions lead to different distributive consequences and create a conflict of interest between agents. Third, if the chosen parametrization admits a continuum of Pareto-efficient outcomes, an additional coordination problem arises-agreeing on a specific point on the Pareto frontier. The paper reconstructs these barriers as a three-step coordination problem in which expectations about later stages affect agents' willingness to enter Kantian cooperation at the outset. On the basis of the results obtained, a program for further formal research is outlined. The findings contribute to understanding the conditions under which Kantian cooperation can be voluntarily adopted and sustainably maintained.

title: When Signals Go Silent: A Regime-switching Theory of Dividend Policy under Systemic Uncertainty
affiliations: Ecole Superieure des Sciences Economiques et Commerciales de Tunis (ESSECT),  Université de Tunis

detail.title: When Signals Go Silent: A Regime-switching Theory of Dividend Policy under Systemic Uncertainty
detail.abstract: Despite six decades of research, the "dividend puzzle" (Black, 1976) remains unresolved because competing explanations, signaling, agency/free cash flow, clientele, life cycle, and catering theories, are typically treated as mutually exclusive and time-invariant. This paper develops the Informational-to-Disciplinary Switching (IDS) framework, a regime-contingent theory proposing that the dominant mechanism governing corporate payout decisions shifts with the level of systemic uncertainty. Under normal conditions, dividends primarily function as costly signals of managers' private information about future earnings (the informational regime). Under heightened systemic uncertainty, financial crises, pandemics, sovereign-debt shocks, aggregate noise erodes the cross-sectional informativeness of dividend signals, and the dominant function of payout shifts toward disciplining managerial discretion over scarce free cash flow, with ownership structure and corporate governance becoming the primary determinants (the disciplinary regime). We formalize this intuition with a deliberately light analytical model featuring a systemic-uncertainty parameter and an endogenous switching threshold, derive six testable propositions, and outline an empirical research design, combining event-study and panel-threshold methods, suited to emerging-market settings where governance heterogeneity and crisis exposure are pronounced. The framework reconciles fragmented strands of the dividend literature within a single dynamic architecture and yields direct implications for investors, boards, and regulators.

title: The Meritorious 'Other': The Interconnection of Merit and Race in EU Migration and Asylum Law
affiliations: , Stockholm School of Economics, Central European University (CEU) and Warsaw School of Economics (SGH)

detail.title: The Meritorious 'Other': The Interconnection of Merit and Race in EU Migration and Asylum Law
detail.abstract: Adopting a law-in-context approach, this article suggests that merit-based migrant selection in the European Union (EU) is implicitly shaped by racial dynamics. With a focus on EU law and more specifically on cases from the Netherlands and Germany, it argues that the growing emphasis on merit enables a limited number of 'racialised others' to counterbalance the structural disadvantages associated with their citizenships, whilst simultaneously legitimising the exclusion of those considered insufficiently meritorious within the same group. By bridging two distinct strands of scholarship-critical analyses of the racial dimensions of migration policy and studies of merit-based selection mechanisms-this article advances existing debates on EU migration and asylum governance. It posits that the normative appeal of merit acts to justify existing hierarchies and to obscure the underlying racialisation processes that sustain them.

title:
Contractual Subordination and Restitution after Breach 
Quantum Meruit for the Defaulting Performer in New York Law
affiliations: Columbia Law School

detail.title:
Contractual Subordination and Restitution after Breach 
Quantum Meruit for the Defaulting Performer in New York Law
detail.abstract: The hardest restitution problem in contract law is not whether breach is wrongful. It is whether the recipient of partial performance has a legal basis for retaining the net benefit of that performance without paying for it. New York law intensifies that problem. On one side, Clark-Fitzpatrick and Corsello make clear that quasi-contract is unavailable where a valid and enforceable contract governs the subject matter and that unjust enrichment is not a fallback whenever ordinary claims fail. On the other side, Farash, Bradkin, substantial-performance doctrine, and UCC § 2-718 reflect an anti-windfall impulse that sometimes allows recovery for requested or retained benefits without enforcing the claimant’s failed contractual theory. New York has not adopted Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 374 as a general rule for breaching performers across contract categories. This article therefore replaces the moral question—should the breacher recover?—with a legal question: does contract, statute, equity, or offset legally justify the recipient’s retention of the net benefit? It argues that New York breaching-party restitution is best understood through contractual subordination. Restitution to a defaulting performer is not categorically barred because the claimant breached, but it is also not freely available whenever the recipient benefited. It is available, if at all, only when subordinate to the parties’ enforceable contract, statutory policy, equitable limitations, and compensatory offsets. The framework has immediate commercial significance. Businesses that want predictable consequences after partial performance, termination, abandonment, or breach must draft expressly for accepted work, payment triggers, offsets, liquidated damages, intellectual-property ownership, and quasi-contract waiver.

title: Quantifying Systemic Topological Fragility: A Geometric Framework for Stress Testing Algorithmic Consensus in Multi-asset Markets

detail.title: Quantifying Systemic Topological Fragility: A Geometric Framework for Stress Testing Algorithmic Consensus in Multi-asset Markets
detail.abstract: The accelerating consolidation of quantitative investment strategies around a narrow set of machine learning architectures and alternative data sources has created a latent class of systemic risk that conventional stochastic risk models are mathematically incapable of detecting. This paper formalises the phenomenon of Algorithmic Consensus Homogenisation (ACH), defined as the convergence of independent trading agents onto statistically equivalent epistemic manifolds, and investigates its consequences for market stability and liquidity resilience. We develop a geometric programme, Topological Finance, that embeds highfrequency limit order book (LOB) data as a multi-dimensional point cloud and monitors the temporal evolution of persistent topological invariants, Fisher information metric contraction, and Ollivier-Ricci curvature to detect structural fragility before it propagates into observable prices. The central theoretical claim is that market crashes are not exogenous surprises but are deterministic Ricci singularities: geometric phase transitions in which the curvature of the market manifold concentrates to a structural breaking point. We validate a 220-tick lead-time advantage over conventional volatility triggers and propose Geometric Circuit Breakers as a regulatory instrument triggered by structural metric decay rather than lagging price movement. The framework delivers actionable contributions to institutional risk management, financial regulation, and the foundations of market efficiency theory.

title: The Welfare Cost of Knowing: Social Comparison of Choice Opportunities

detail.title: The Welfare Cost of Knowing: Social Comparison of Choice Opportunities
detail.abstract: Does learning that others have superior choice opportunities reduce welfare when one's own options remain unchanged? Using an incentivized experiment with 448 participants, I randomly assign participants to identical small choice sets while varying only information about others' access to larger sets. Participants informed about differential access experience substantial welfare effects: satisfaction decreases by 0.284 points (p = 0.058), choice stability falls by 28.5 percentage points (p < 0.001), and willingness to retain chosen items drops by 16.9 percentage points (p = 0.017). These opportunity-based social comparison effects-representing a distinct welfare channel-completely offset the welfare gains from actual choice expansion. The results imply that when differences in access become visible, transparency itself can impose utility losses comparable to the gains from expanded options. This reveals a fundamental tension between information disclosure and individual welfare in digitally mediated markets.

title: Two Faced: A Wellness-informed Framework for Therapeutic Beauty Practice | Presence, Nonverbal Intelligence, and the Ministry of the Chair

detail.title: Two Faced: A Wellness-informed Framework for Therapeutic Beauty Practice | Presence, Nonverbal Intelligence, and the Ministry of the Chair
detail.abstract: This paper introduces Two Faced, a wellness-informed framework for therapeutic beauty practice developed by R. Nicole Smith, a licensed minister and credentialed Marriage and Family Therapist. Two Faced reframes the beauty chair as a site of intentional interruption-a space where clients are invited to step out of autopilot, be witnessed in their full complexity, and experience practitioner presence that is clinically informed without constituting clinical treatment. Drawing on graduate training in trauma-informed care, nonverbal communication, family systems theory, and human development, the framework proposes that beauty practitioners equipped with therapeutic literacy can function as meaningful points of contact in a client's healing ecology-not as therapists, but as witnesses. The paper explores the cultural and theological dimensions of the "two faces" women carry, articulates the clinical competencies that inform Two Faced practice, establishes a protective language system that maintains scope of practice integrity, and positions wellness-informed beauty work as a legitimate interdisciplinary contribution at the intersection of practical theology, somatic awareness, and community care.

title: Firms' Partisan Alignment and Economic Expectations

detail.title: Firms' Partisan Alignment and Economic Expectations
detail.abstract: This paper examines whether firms' partisan alignment with the incumbent president shapes their economic optimism, and whether such alignment-driven optimism translates into firms' stated business plans. I measure firms' partisan preferences by aggregating executives' political donation behavior using the DIME database. I then define partisan alignment based on whether a firm's partisan preference matches that of the sitting president. Using firmlevel survey data from the Duke CFO Survey, I estimate panel regressions with firm and year fixed effects to exploit within-firm variation in partisan alignment over time. I find that partisan alignment significantly boosts firms' optimism about both the aggregate economy and their own financial prospects, while partisan preference alone has no predictive power absent alignment. However, this alignment-driven optimism does not appear to carry over into firms' stated business plans, even though general optimism itself is shown to be a significant predictor of stated plans in the data. These patterns are suggestive of a parallel to the householdlevel cheerleading effect documented by Mian, Sufi and Khoshkhou (2023). The findings extend the literature on partisan bias in economic expectations from households to firms, suggesting that similar mechanisms may operate at the firm level.

title:
The Abstraction Path of the Labor Theory of Value: Variable Demotion, the Multiple Realizability of the
Determinant, and the Reality Constraint Principle
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title:
The Abstraction Path of the Labor Theory of Value: Variable Demotion, the Multiple Realizability of the
Determinant, and the Reality Constraint Principle
detail.abstract: The labor theory of value (LTV) builds a highly unied framework of value determination around socially necessary labor time (SNLT) as its core explanatory variable. Yet at the nal explanatory level, real productive variablescapital, technology, institutions, organization, and material conditionsare systematically reduced to derivative forms of labor, yielding a singlecause, vertically reductive abstraction path. This paper proposes a Reality Constraint Principle and situates it within the philosophy-of-science traditions of Popper, Lakatos, and Kuhn. On this basis it advances a limited but pointed methodological argument: with respect to the function of explaining price coordination, the determinant of value is multiply realizable any real factor that directly participates in production can occupy the formal position of LTV's unique source of valueand demonstrates this through a minimal, computable construction. It follows that labor's special status is a theoretical stipulation rather than a theoretical necessity. The paper further proposes a Realistic Production Cross-Section Model as a methodological contrast tool, showing the form a framework takes when abstraction preserves the independent standing of the main real variables. The aim is methodological critique, not the construction of a substitute theory of value; the conclusions are strictly conned to the testability of the abstraction path and pass no verdict on the proposition of surplus value or exploitation as such.

detail.abstract: How do uncontrollable shocks affect preferences for redistribution? This paper examines whether long-run exposure to natural hazards shifts distributive preferences toward greater support for income equality and away from stronger incentives for individual effort. I link individual-level data from the joint European Values Study and World Values Survey to country-level measures of exposure to droughts, floods, and extreme temperatures. The analysis covers 80,701 respondents nested within 737 local regions and 56 countries/territories. Using multilevel hierarchical models, and confirming the results with OLS and ordered logit specifications, I find that greater hazard exposure is associated with significantly stronger support for making incomes more equal and weaker support for effort-based distributive preferences. Interaction analyses show that this association is strongest among respondents who initially place greater weight on hard work, among higher-income groups, and in countries characterized by stronger institutional quality and higher preexisting inequality. These patterns are consistent with political-economy accounts in which exogenous shocks alter beliefs about fairness, increase perceived vulnerability, and strengthen demand for collective insurance and compensation. The findings contribute to the political economy of redistribution by showing that distributive preferences are shaped not only by income, ideology, and mobility expectations, but also by lived exposure to uncontrollable risk.

title: High-Entropy Intelligence: From Materials to Markets to Minds toward AGI
affiliations: , ,  and National Chung Hsing University

detail.title: High-Entropy Intelligence: From Materials to Markets to Minds toward AGI
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces Behavioral Consensus Theory (BCT) as a new solution to the longstanding
problem of financial market complexity. BCT is grounded in High-Entropy Intelligence (HEI)
principles and directly addresses Ashby's Law of Requisite Variety, which states that only
variety can absorb variety—meaning controllers must possess internal complexity matching the
systems they regulate. Financial markets, as high-entropy emergent systems, have historically
evaded low-entropy models precisely because those models violate Ashby's Law by lacking
sufficient configurational diversity. BCT is conceptually inspired by high-entropy alloying (HEA)
in materials science, where heterogeneous components achieve superior emergent properties
through entropic integration and entanglement.
BCT proposes three synergistic consensus mechanisms that jointly govern price formation in
complex markets: (1) Psychological Causality Consensus Effect—prices arise from a quantitative
equilibrium shaped by rational and irrational forces, incorporating memory, anchoring, attention,
and other behavioral constraints. (2) Physical Equivalence Consensus Effect—market dynamics
follow quantum-mechanical analogues, including price orbitals, tunneling behaviors, state
transitions, and symmetry-preserving and symmetry-breaking mechanisms. (3) Spatiotemporal
Entanglement Consensus Effect—price dynamic prediction accuracy is enhanced by determining
the best representative reduced entanglement derived from prior consensuses' treatment across
multiple temporal, structural, and spatial layers of market information.
By satisfying Ashby's Law through high configurational diversity across behavioral, physical, and
spatiotemporal dimensions, BCT achieves the requisite variety necessary to match market
complexity. Using rigorous mathematical formalization and empirical tests on PEAD, we demonstrate that these consensus effects jointly resolve persistent anomalies such as congestion,
trending, jump discontinuities, volatility clustering, and Post-Earnings Announcement Drift
(PEAD). The framework establishes Psychoeconophysics as a transdisciplinary field unifying
behavioral finance with modern physics and provides a foundational architecture for Artificial
Finance Intelligence (AFI) systems. Most critically, BCT delivers the first unified quantitative
model that integrates rational and irrational decision processes within a single coherent system—
resolving the century-long divide between rational expectations theory and behavioral finance.
Our findings suggest that High-Entropy frameworks can offer superior modeling power for
complex adaptive systems well beyond financial markets, with implications for artificial general
intelligence and multi-scale systems science.

title: The Truman Theory: A Formal Synthesis of Cosmic Quarantine, Simulation, and Managed-civilization Hypotheses
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Truman Theory: A Formal Synthesis of Cosmic Quarantine, Simulation, and Managed-civilization Hypotheses
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the Truman Theory, a formal synthesis of three frameworks that are usually treated
separately: John Ball's zoo hypothesis, Nick Bostrom's simulation argument, and the cultural model supplied by
The Truman Show. The central claim is not that any single UAP report proves extraterrestrial management, nor
that human history can be reduced to a controlled experiment. The claim is narrower and more rigorous. Given
the age of the universe, the abundance of planets, the likely existence of civilizations far older than ours, the
recurrent emergence of power structures in complex adaptive systems, and the reported concentration of
anomalous aerospace phenomena around nuclear and strategic sites, Earth may be best modeled as a protected,
observed, and occasionally managed primitive civilization. The model treats direct public contact as a boundary
condition rather than an oversight. It also treats secrecy less as a human conspiracy than as an epistemic feature
of managed non-interference: once the subject civilization knows the full context of observation, the object of
study changes. The paper distinguishes established science, logical extrapolation, and speculative inference,
then develops the Truman Theory as a hypothesis with philosophical, astrobiological, political, and existential-
risk implications.

title: External Accountability and Fiscal Transparency in Hierarchical Governance: Evidence from Chinese Cities
affiliations: Tsinghua University, Peking University and Development Research Center of the State Council

detail.title: External Accountability and Fiscal Transparency in Hierarchical Governance: Evidence from Chinese Cities
detail.abstract: Fiscal transparency is a cornerstone of public governance, yet its determinants remain contested. This article argues that fiscal transparency is primarily driven by external accountability-market discipline and administrative hierarchy-rather than societal demand or local leaders' initiative, especially in systems lacking electoral accountability. Using an original dataset of fiscal disclosures from 294 Chinese cities (2013-2021), we construct a comprehensive fiscal transparency index covering institutional, on-budget, and off-budget dimensions. The analysis shows that market exposure and hierarchical oversight significantly increase fiscal transparency, while local societal and leadership factors have limited effects. These findings highlight the central role of institutional accountability in shaping fiscal transparency in hierarchical governance contexts.

title: The Erosion of Territorial Sovereignty in Venezuela: From the Hybrid Armed State to Multilateral Kinetic Intervention Lise Working Paper Series | Security Governance & Transnational Law

detail.title: The Erosion of Territorial Sovereignty in Venezuela: From the Hybrid Armed State to Multilateral Kinetic Intervention Lise Working Paper Series | Security Governance & Transnational Law
detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the historical collapse and systemic fragmentation of territorial sovereignty in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, culminating in the recent kinetic neutralization of Héctor Rusthenford Guerrero Flores (alias "Niño Guerrero"), leader of the Tren de Aragua criminal cartel, in southern Venezuela through coordinated multilateral action. Confronting the constitutional text with empirical indicators of security governance, this analysis traces how the Venezuelan state systematically abdicated its Weberian monopoly on the legitimate use of physical force. This paper argues that the loss of sovereignty was not a sudden institutional failure, but rather a deliberate process of state hybridization that occurred across three distinct historical phases: the concession of sanctuary to Colombian insurgent groups (FARC/ELN), the deep institutional infiltration of foreign intelligence and logistical apparatuses (Cuba/Iran/Hezbollah), and the formal delegation of local territorial control to domestic criminal structures (Pranatos and Megabandas). Examined under the lens of the Venezuelan Constitution, UN declarations, and international criminal doctrine, the paper concludes that the multilateral operation against the Tren de Aragua leadership provides definitive legal and empirical proof of a fragmented sovereignty and criminal governance, transforming Venezuela from a classic Westphalian sovereign state into a contested regional security theater.

title: A New Framework for Understanding Consent in Tort Law
affiliations: University of California, Irvine School of Law

detail.title: A New Framework for Understanding Consent in Tort Law

publicationDetails.detailsText: UC Irvine School of Law Research Paper No. 2026-12
publicationDetails.journalName: University of California, Irvine School of Law & Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Intentional torts such as battery, assault, and false imprisonment identify wrongful conduct that violates a person’s rights by intentionally and unjustifiably intruding upon the person’s autonomy, thereby causing physical harm, emotional harm, or dignitary offense. But when that person actually consents to such conduct, consent vitiates the wrong and justifiably precludes liability.

Yet consent is controversial and divisive. In the context of sexual conduct, consent provokes especially intense contemporary debate. In other contexts, too, disagreement abounds about the type of consent that is legally effective. Although the concept of consent in criminal law has been extensively explored, few scholars have thoroughly analyzed consent in tort law.

This article demonstrates that controversies about the proper content and scope of consent rest in part on a failure to appreciate the distinct doctrinal categories of consent that preclude tort liability. By distinguishing these categories and demonstrating their significance and interrelationship, this article permits a clearer articulation of the criteria for resolving the controversies and renders the controversies much more tractable.

The article identifies three different categories of consent that are independently sufficient to preclude tort liability and also notes two additional categories that are highly problematic. The first category is actual consent, or willingness that an actor engages in otherwise tortious conduct. The second is apparent consent, which refers to cases in which the actor reasonably believes, perhaps mistakenly, that the plaintiff actually consents. The third category is hypothetical or presumed consent, a category that courts and scholars have rarely identified and explained, except in a narrow subcategory (the emergency doctrine). Here, even if the actor knows that the plaintiff does not actually consent (e.g., because the plaintiff is asleep or unconscious or merely surprised by the actor’s conduct), the actor is sometimes justified in proceeding, so long as the actor has no reason to believe that the plaintiff would not have actually consented if the actor had requested such consent. A fourth possible category is implied-in-law or constructive consent, under which courts (in rare cases) preclude tort liability even if the plaintiff expresses objection to the actor’s conduct. I argue that this category should be jettisoned entirely. And a fifth possible category, implied consent simpliciter, is too vague and indiscriminate to be useful.

This framework is applied to numerous concrete scenarios, many drawn from the recently adopted Restatement Third, Torts: Intentional Torts to Persons. A separate section applies the analysis to contemporary controversies about the proper scope of consent to sexual conduct, including the question whether the bright-line rules “NO means NO” and “only YES means YES” (or affirmative consent) should be adopted.

The article is both a descriptive account of the concepts that are explicit or implicit in tort cases, and a normative account of the categories of consent that are most useful and justifiable to employ, consistent with the role of consent in tort doctrine and theory.

title: Pageants and the President: The Liability of Celebrity Politicians

detail.title: Pageants and the President: The Liability of Celebrity Politicians
detail.abstract: We study when celebrity status becomes a liability for politicians once a scandal breaks, using the leak of the Access Hollywood tape during the 2016 U.S. presidential campaign and Donald Trump's prior two-decade ownership of the Miss USA pageant. Exploiting cohort-by-county variation in voters' pre-scandal exposure to Trump-as-the-pageant-owner, we find that the scandal produced a sharper attitudinal and electoral shift among voters with greater prior exposure, with the more exposed counties experiencing an additional decline in Trump's 2016 vote share. Our findings suggest voters' prior exposure to a candidate shapes how they attend to and interpret later political information.

title: Dual Specialisation or Divergent Paths? Sectoral Patterns of Tourism and Technology across European NUTS-3 Regions
