detail.title: Dual Specialisation or Divergent Paths? Sectoral Patterns of Tourism and Technology across European NUTS-3 Regions
detail.abstract: This paper examines the coexistence of tourism and technology across European NUTS-3 regions using Eurostat employment data for 2003-2023. A relative specialisation index is constructed to classify regions according to their sectoral profiles, and a Bai-Perron test identifies a structural break around 2010, allowing comparison between pre-and post-shock periods. The results show strong persistence in regional specialisation patterns, alongside moderate shifts away from dual-specialised configurations towards more asymmetric structures. Low-specialisation profiles dominate, particularly among lower-income regions, while higher-income regions are more frequently associated with technology-intensive and dual-specialisation patterns. Structural changes are sector-specific and income-dependent, with greater variability in tourism among lower-income regions and stronger technological dynamics in higher-income regions. Overall, tourism and technology are not mutually exclusive, but coexist within differentiated regional trajectories shaped by initial conditions and sectoral capabilities.

title: Climate Stress and International Migration from MENA
affiliations: ,  and Migration Policy Group

detail.title: Climate Stress and International Migration from MENA
detail.abstract:
Existing research on the drivers of international migration is constrained by incomplete
measurement of volumes, directions and country coverage. Most studies focus on recent
decades, a narrow set of OECD destinations or a single flow type, even though categories
are blurred, new destinations have emerged and many developing countries now host large
migrant populations. Recent work suggests that migration drivers are best understood within
a broader migration system rather than in isolation. However, even in this newer literature,
long-run historical ties, such as deep ancestry links or very old migrant stocks, are still
rarely analyzed jointly with contemporary drivers and environmental pressures in a unified
empirical framework.
      In this paper, we focus on MENA countries and use bilateral flow estimates from Abel
(2018) in a gravity framework to analyse how environmental stress interacts with the broader
social, political, and historical structures that organise migration. We distinguish fast-onset
shocks, measured by the number of people affected by floods and storms, from slow-onset
anomalies, captured by 12-month SPEI indicators for unusually dry and unusually wet conditions.
These origin-year shocks have been analyzed in a rich context of civil conflict,
development, urbanization, and agrarian exposure, and we further augmented the study
with historical migrant stocks around 1960 and a new ancestry stock measure we developed,
reflects historical ties built up in the Colonial Era. This study is one of the first to
incorporate deep ancestry-based ties into an empirical analysis of migration from MENA.
      Our results show that fast-onset disasters affect emigration from MENA in a non-linear
way: small and moderate events are largely absorbed locally, while very severe shocks lead to
sharp increases in cross-border outflows. Deviations from normal moisture in either direction,
whether drought or excess rainfall, are also associated with higher emigration. In addition,
migrant stocks and ancestry links are strong and robust predictors of where migrants move,
even after we control for other conditions.

title: Which Alignment Pays? Fiscal Patronage, Electoral Returns, and Local Party Dominance in Taiwan
affiliations: Hong Kong Metropolitan University and National Chengchi University (NCCU) - College of Social Sciences

detail.title: Which Alignment Pays? Fiscal Patronage, Electoral Returns, and Local Party Dominance in Taiwan
detail.abstract: Candidates in multilevel party systems face party labels that do not carry uniform value across territory. This article asks which forms of dominant-party alignment pay for regional legislative candidates. Drawing on candidate-election, candidate-panel, regional-dominance, and county-year fiscal data from Taiwan, it tests whether alignment is associated with fiscal-transfer gains, current electoral returns, later career continuation, and distinct payoff patterns in indigenous constituencies. The evidence indicates that regional-dominant alignment is associated with the clearest electoral and career returns, whereas national-tier-only alignment is weaker and fiscal-transfer evidence is limited. Indigenous constituencies display a different payoff structure, especially around independent candidacy. The article contributes to party politics by disaggregating alignment into competing payoff mechanisms and by showing that local organizational dominance can matter more for candidate viability than national dominance alone.

title: Beyond De-risking: Strategic Dependence as a Geopolitical Externality

detail.title: Beyond De-risking: Strategic Dependence as a Geopolitical Externality
detail.abstract:
Economic security has become a central concern in contemporary political economy, yet existing debates often focus on identifying vulnerabilities rather than explaining why strategically significant dependencies emerge and persist. This paper argues that strategic dependence should be understood as a geopolitical externality. Firms organize production and sourcing decisions according to private incentives that reward efficiency, specialization, and cost reduction, but some of the resulting risks are borne by consumers, governments, critical infrastructures, and society more broadly. Markets may therefore generate more strategic dependence than is socially optimal.

Drawing on the economics of externalities, the paper conceptualizes strategic dependence as a form of geopolitical market failure and reframes economic security as a problem of governing interdependence rather than reducing it. It develops a Strategic Dependence Index based on concentration, substitutability, and systemic impact, and applies the framework to rare-earth supply chains and advanced semiconductors. The analysis shows how strategically significant dependencies can be distinguished from ordinary commercial interdependence and identifies conditions under which public intervention may be justified.

title: AEF-Econ: Toward Plug-and-Play Socioeconomic Foundation Embeddings from AlphaEarth for Urban Remote Sensing
affiliations: Wuhan University, Wuhan University, Wuhan University, Wuhan University, Wuhan University, Wuhan University, Wuhan University, Wuhan University, Wuhan University and Wuhan University

detail.title: AEF-Econ: Toward Plug-and-Play Socioeconomic Foundation Embeddings from AlphaEarth for Urban Remote Sensing
detail.abstract: AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) unify global remote sensing foundation embeddings through multimodal self-supervised learning, but their pretraining focuses on physical land-surface signals, limiting plug-and-play use in socioeconomic tasks. We integrate seven heterogeneous data streams across 36 Chinese cities over eight years-AEF embeddings, population, nighttime lights, remote sensing indices, points of interest (POIs), urban morphology, and cross-lingual text-and construct CHN-Econ, a socioeconomic benchmark with 16 labels in three categories. We conduct 31 controlled experiments along five axes: fusion architecture, self-supervised objective, text integration, embedding dimensionality, and normalization. Used alone as a linear probe, AEF achieves R² values of only 0.301 for cross-region and 0.160 for cross-tier evaluation. The five-axis ablated backbone improves these scores to 0.832 and 0.671, respectively, but reveals that lowdimensional semantic streams are consistently suppressed by high-dimensional streams under shared reconstruction. To address this bottleneck, we propose Capacity-Adaptive Reconstruction (CAR), replacing shared reconstruction with per-stream decoders and stream-level losses to mitigate inter-stream capacity competition. CAR further raises cross-region and cross-tier R² to 0.848 and 0.693, and restores collapsed labels from negative R² to a stable range. Using CAR, we infer 14.4 million pixels across 36 cities and eight years and release AEF-Econ, including 128d and 64d compressed versions. Self-diagnostics and case studies show that AEF-Econ captures cross-city hierarchies and intra-urban spatial organization under unsupervised settings, providing a socioeconomic remote sensing foundation embedding complementary to AEF physical embeddings.

title: Data Under-Utilization with Privacy Concerns: Theory and Regulation

detail.abstract: Against the backdrop of extensive research on abuse of data, some empirical evidence suggests that platforms may not fully use their own level of data spontaneously. We model data governance as a platform-level service design problem: differentiated platforms choose data-utilization intensity, which raises cross-side network benefits for users of core platform services but imposes privacy costs on participating consumers. Under homogeneity and no privacy spillover, equilibrium intensity is systematically below the first-best because data-driven quality improvements benefit inframarginal participants while platforms monetize mainly through marginal participation (a Spence-Weyl wedge in data intensity). In the benchmark closed form, data intensity is independent of horizontal differentiation. The model also delivers a sharp pricing-structure implication: privacy-cost shocks pass through to consumer versus merchant fees according to cross-side externality asymmetry. We also conduct comparative static and welfare analysis, and compare two common regulations: command-and-control utilization standards may nonetheless reduce consumer surplus once platforms reoptimize access fees, whereas well-designed data pooling can improve consumer surplus locally when competition is strong. Finally, we extend the model to general privacy-type distributions, aggregate ecosystem privacy externalities jointly with platform heterogeneity in monetization efficiency, and free entry. This paper provides a new perspective on platform data governance through participation, pricing, and privacy.

detail.title: Carbon Pricing and Investment
detail.abstract: How does carbon pricing affect investment in brown firms? During the period 2000-2019, the effective cost of emitting carbon rose by about 400 percent for Swedish manufacturing firms. Despite lower operating margins, high-emission firms significantly increased both total capital investment and the share of investment dedicated to abatement. The response is concentrated among firms with strong internal financial capacity. We find no comparable investment increase in lower-emitting firms or in high-emission industries outside of Sweden. Our results show that pricing CO2 emissions at a sufficiently high level can incentivize brown firms to make green investments.

title: An Analysis of Intellectual Property Rights in Nigeria’s Fashion Industry

detail.title: An Analysis of Intellectual Property Rights in Nigeria’s Fashion Industry

keywords: Counterfeiting and Piracy Fashion Industry Brand Protection

detail.abstract:
The protection of intellectual property rights in Nigeria's fashion sector is examined in this article, with particular attention to copyright, industrial design, trademarks, patent law, and the common law action of passing off. It contends that while Nigerian law offers a variety of legal safeguards, these regimes are both individually and collectively insufficient to completely protect commercial innovation and fashion originality.
The report also emphasizes issues like digital infringement, counterfeiting and the territorial nature of intellectual property rights. It comes to the conclusion that in order to improve the protection of innovation and investment in Nigeria's fashion industry, more enforcement and increased awareness are required.

title: Can Automation Offset Population Decline? Occupational Imbalances in a Shrinking Workforce
affiliations: and Bank of Korea

detail.title: Can Automation Offset Population Decline? Occupational Imbalances in a Shrinking Workforce
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether automation can mitigate the labor-market effects of population decline and how this mitigation differs across occupations. Korea's working-age population is projected to fall by about 11 percent between 2024 and 2034. Holding current occupational demand fixed, we first project occupation-level labor-supply imbalances using Korean population projections and age-by-occupation employment data. We then estimate occupation-level automation probabilities by applying a large language model (LLM) to O*NET task statements and mapping the resulting task-level measures to Korean occupations. Automation can substantially reduce the aggregate labor shortfall, but it does not eliminate occupational imbalance because automation potential is only weakly aligned with projected demographic shortages. The main implication is therefore compositional: population decline changes the distribution of labor scarcity, while automation changes where shortages persist and where surplus pressure emerges. With sufficiently rapid AI progress, the same framework implies that the policy problem may shift from aggregate labor shortage to the distribution of labor surplus across occupations.

title: AI-driven Versus Econometric Supply Chain Simulation for Nearshoring Resilience in Mexico
affiliations: UNAM and Universidad Nacional Autonoma de Mexico

detail.title: AI-driven Versus Econometric Supply Chain Simulation for Nearshoring Resilience in Mexico
detail.abstract: This study applies explainable artificial intelligence-gradient boosting and SHAP value decomposition-to evaluate policies that strengthen supply chain resilience, a core dimension of economic sustainability, across Mexico's 32 states as a representative emerging-market economy facing distinct infrastructure and financial frictions. Since 2023, Mexico has surpassed China as the leading source of US goods imports, yet infrastructure constraints threaten regional capacity to capture the nearshoring wave. We compare two agent-based models sharing identical architecture (32 states, 2017-2024, twelve resilience scenarios) that differ only in the production engine: a Cobb-Douglas specification estimated via panel econometrics versus a gradient boosting model (R 2 = 0.91). The ML engine outperforms the econometric benchmark on five of nine empirical moments with no total failures, produces more consistent policy rankings across 50 random seeds (68% convergence on supplier development as top-ranked versus a scattered distribution), and-via SHAP-discovers nonlinear infrastructure thresholds invisible to the constant-elasticity specification. The econometric model shows greater sensitivity to extreme shocks, but this reflects a binary recovery artefact rather than nuanced dynamics. For AI-powered supply chain analytics in emerging markets, the ML engine is the recommended default; the comparison identifies specific extrapolation boundaries where caution is warranted.

detail.abstract: I wanted to find out whether what CEOs post on X actually makes their company's stock move more than usual. I then measured how much more or less each stock moved in the two days after each post compared to normal. When I ran the regression the only thing that came back significant was the overall market volatility index called the VIX (p=0.015). title: Information Selling under Prior Disagreement
affiliations: University of Colorado at Boulder - Department of Economics and

detail.title: Information Selling under Prior Disagreement
detail.abstract: We study monopolistic information selling under prior disagreement and limited intertemporal commitment. A Seller offers experiments to a Buyer over multiple periods. Under a common prior, sequential information selling does not increase revenue. By contrast, under prior disagreement, revenue maximization requires sequential selling. Moreover, for generic prior beliefs, the Seller’s revenue strictly increases with the length of the interaction. Yet, expected revenue remains bounded by the payoff achievable under commitment with non-negative state-contingent payments. In some environments, optimal information-selling strategies involve an initial free experiment. Paternalistic policies that restrict free samples or gradual information provision improve the Buyer’s welfare.

detail.abstract:
This research examines the effect of competition law and national security–driven investment screening on mergers and acquisitions between the United Kingdom and the United States. It analyses agency guidance, statutory frameworks, and case studies using a doctrinal and comparative methodology.

The study finds that both jurisdictions engage similar substantive standards; however, there is a sharp difference between their procedural and institutional structures. The UK allows the Competition and Markets Authority to interfere flexibly through its voluntary and non-suspensory merger regime, especially in innovation-driven markets. The US system, however being anchored in Hart–Scott–Rodino pre-notification and judicial enforcement, showcases greater scepticism towards speculative theories of harm and demands higher evidentiary thresholds. In national security, the UK’s National Security and Investment Act 2021 and the US’s CFIUS regime both give regulatory agencies extensive discretion, extending well beyond traditional antitrust concerns.

The research contributes significantly to legal scholarship in many ways. Primarily, it deals with a post-Brexit gap by contrasting the two jurisdictions’ approaches to merger control and investment screening systematically. Secondly, it highlights how uncertainty and extraterritorial effects in high-value transactions are created because of overlapping competition and security regimes. Finally, it proposes policy recommendations such as clearer guidance on innovation-based theories of harm, improved cross-border harmonisation of remedies, and better transparency in security assessments.

detail.abstract: There is a philosophical debate about whether the use of biomedical enhancements to promote or sustain love in romantic relationships is compatible with the desirability of such love. We argue that enhancements are problematic in this respect only if they substantially replace the causal role of the beloved's identity in generating the lover's disposition to care. When enhancements remove psychological impediments to seeing the beloved "as they really are" without introducing new (significant or overriding) inauthentic causes of love, they do not reduce the value of the love between the lover and beloved. In this paper, we discuss three conditions for love to be an intrinsically valuable good and the causal role of the beloved's identity for each of them. We show that the fundamental desirability of love understood in terms of these three conditions does not depend on whether enhancements are used, but on whether the identity of the beloved continues to play the right causal role. Enhancements can help us preserve valuable relationships and support the causes of love that are already in place. Finally, even if relatively less desirable than unenhanced love, enhanced love can still remain valuable and desirable in absolute terms.

title: The Citizens Standard: The Structural Buyer — Asset-Market Dynamics, Price Discovery, and Universal Ownership
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Citizens Standard: The Structural Buyer — Asset-Market Dynamics, Price Discovery, and Universal Ownership
detail.abstract: The Citizens Standard makes the public a permanent, price-insensitive net buyer of total-market equity — on the order of the annual K1+K2 deposit flow. The standing objection, voiced informally by critics and stated formally as an open problem in the macroeconomic model (Neo Solon, 2026e, §8), is that such a buyer must do one of four things: inflate asset prices without limit, destroy price discovery, leak into consumer-price inflation, or concentrate corporate control in a single state-adjacent vehicle. This paper shows that none of the four holds under the architecture's design, and locates precisely where each effect is real but bounded. The analysis separates the flow the buyer adds each period from the stock it accumulates over time. On the flow side: the valuation premium converges to a finite fixed point A*/φ; in steady state the flow is intermediated through primary equity issuance and therefore funds real capital formation rather than perpetual repricing; and the consumption leak into the transactional circuit is bounded by the marginal propensity to consume out of asset wealth (≈ 3%). On the stock side: cumulative ownership plateaus through decumulation rather than rising to one, price discovery is preserved above an active-float threshold, the cost-of-capital effect is allocation-neutral within a total market index, the index is capture-resistant when mechanical and constitutionally locked, and a mirror-voting rule renders the citizen stake economically real but control-neutral. Each result is conditional on stated quantities; the one that runs against the framework in the present US regime — the net equity-supply response φ — is secured by a buyback constraint this paper identifies as a required complement to the architecture and carries as its baseline; the framework adopts it as the payout-neutrality safeguard of the architecture (Neo-Solon, 2026a, §19.6) and the graduated repurchase charge of the statutory pathway (2026d, §10).

title: Spiked Eigenvalue and Spectral Gap Estimation under Heavy Tails via Truncated Sample Covariance
affiliations: WorldQuant University

detail.title: Spiked Eigenvalue and Spectral Gap Estimation under Heavy Tails via Truncated Sample Covariance
detail.abstract:
I develop a random matrix theory (RMT) framework for estimating spiked eigenvalues and the spectral gap δpop—the minimum distance between consecutive spiked eigenvalues and between the smallest spike and the bulk—of the covariance operator of heavy-tailed random vectors. I work with a centered, vector-truncated robust covariance estimator Σˆ = n −1 P(Yi − Y¯ )(Yi − Y¯ ) ⊤ with Yi = Ψτ (X˜ i) = X˜ i min(1, τ /∥X˜ i∥). The key observation is that Σˆ is exactly a sample covariance matrix of i.i.d. bounded random vectors satisfying ∥Yi∥ ≤ τ . Since bounded vectors have finite moments of all orders, the i.i.d. vector Marčenko–Pastur theorem of Bai & Zhou (2008)—which permits arbitrary dependence among coordinates—applies directly, with no need for new heavy-tailed RMT. The cost of truncation is a bias of order M/τ p−2 between the truncated and true population covariance.
I prove: (i) the empirical spectral distribution of Σˆ converges to the standard Marčenko–Pastur law; (ii) spiked eigenvalues converge at rate Op(εn √ log n) with εn = n −(p−2)/(2(p−1)), via Weyl’s inequality and a two-term matrix Bernstein bound; (iii) a bootstrap-based factor selection procedure is consistent without knowledge of the tail index; (iv) the spectral gap estimator ˆδpop converges at rate εn √ log n. I show that truncation restores operator-norm consistency, bypassing the nonlinear BBP spike mapping that governs the standard sample covariance (Lemma 5.1), so that ∥Σˆ − Σ∥2 → 0 despite d/n → c > 0. The estimated gap feeds into a dimensionless instability constant Kˆ inst with bootstrap-based uncertainty quantification, enabling early-warning diagnostics for structural changes in the covariance spectrum.

title: Pluralizing the PHOSITA in Patent Law

detail.title: Pluralizing the PHOSITA in Patent Law
detail.abstract:
Patent law adjudicates invention through a singular fiction: the person having ordinary skill in the art (PHOSITA). That construct now misfires. Courts endow it with encyclopedic knowledge yet cabin its inventiveness. They insist on one mind while modern innovation unfolds through teams and in complex networks. This Article contends that a unitary PHOSITA distorts the patent law's architecture. 
Recent patent doctrine has upgraded the PHOSITA's cognition without fully rethinking the subject who thinks. Creativity does not scale with credentials alone and rarely resides in solitary actors. Data reveal team-dominant innovation. Social science reveals collaboration can catalyze or corrode insight depending on structure. Moreover, collaboration is not the full story; competition also influences innovation. The PHOSITA, conceived as a solitary being, cannot plausibly proxy this environment.
Courts and commentators largely treat collaboration as a knowledge‑aggregation device rather than a creativity‑modulating force. This Article proposes a pluralized PHOSITA along two orthogonal dimensions. The collaborative dimension distinguishes asynchronous aggregation of prior art from synchronous teamwork. The competitive dimension considers actual races and, more provocatively, introduces “potential competition,” defined as the total population capable of inventing the innovation—thereby recasting inventions in fields with few qualified artisans as less “inevitable” despite high skill. Tested against obviousness theories—“but-for” inducement, cognitive difficulty, and probabilistic success—the framework better filters trivial advances without demanding unadministrable counterfactuals. It preserves the cognitive lens while importing insights from alternative frameworks.

title: An Image Processing-Based Hybrid MCDM Framework for Urban Seismic Vulnerability Prioritization in Resource-Constrained Environments: A Case Study of Dhaka
affiliations: , Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) and Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET)

detail.title: An Image Processing-Based Hybrid MCDM Framework for Urban Seismic Vulnerability Prioritization in Resource-Constrained Environments: A Case Study of Dhaka
detail.abstract: In resource-constrained and densely populated cities like Dhaka, emergency response capabilities following a major earthquake are likely to face significant limitations. Hence, prioritization and rescue resource allocation become a major challenge in effective disaster management. To address the issue, this study proposes a practical framework for ranking residential areas on their seismic vulnerability based on structural, demographic, and systemic factors. Unlike conventional MCDM approaches that rely heavily on directly assigned criterion values, this study integrates image processing techniques that capture the underlying geospatial patterns relevant to the seismic vulnerability of an area and predict criterion scores of the influencing factors. The relative importances of the influencing factors were determined using the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (Fuzzy AHP), allowing expert judgment and uncertainty to be incorporated into the weighting process. An exhaustive satellite image dataset was created so that the feature extraction model is able to predict the criteria-specific scores accurately, which are then used as inputs in the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) algorithm to rank areas by their post-earthquake vulnerability. The proposed methodology was applied to five different areas in Dhaka, and the results obtained showed its effectiveness in distinguishing variations in seismic vulnerability.

title:
From Ruin to Renewal: 
Turning Floods into Engines of Transformation

detail.title:
From Ruin to Renewal: 
Turning Floods into Engines of Transformation
detail.abstract: This study extends the classic Solow-Swan growth model to explore how the reconstruction of capital after major floods shapes Pakistan's long-term economic growth. The model divides total capital into three key components-traditional, modern, and human capital-to reflect the structural diversity of Pakistan's economy. Floods are introduced as sudden external shocks that damage these forms of capital differently, disrupting the pace of recovery and future growth. The analysis shows that when post-flood rebuilding focuses mainly on traditional capital, such as housing and basic infrastructure, short-term recovery occurs but long-run growth remains limited due to low technological progress. In contrast, reconstruction that also strengthens modern and human capital-through investment in technology, industry, and education-leads to higher productivity and long-run economic growth. The findings suggest that Pakistan's recovery from floods is not just about rebuilding what was lost, but about investing smarter in what can sustain future development. The study concludes by emphasizing the importance of balanced and forwardlooking reconstruction policies, such as the Twin Capital Reconstruction (TCR) Program, whereby budget allocation towards rebuilding capital in a flood-affected economy should have a fixed proportion diverted towards investments in modern and human capital, alongside traditional capital, so as to ensure long-term growth.

detail.abstract:
This paper examines the evolution of UEFA financial governance in European club
football and uses the UEFA Club Financial Control Body as a reference point for a
broader discussion on regulatory asymmetries within the football ecosystem. Over the
last decade and a half, UEFA has developed a sophisticated system of club licensing,
financial monitoring, cost control, investigative procedures, settlement agreements, and
graduated sanctions. The Club Financial Control Body has become the institutional
core of this model. It is designed to preserve financial sustainability, protect creditors,
discourage structural deficits, and promote competitive integrity among clubs
participating in UEFA competitions.
The paper argues that the UEFA financial control model is advanced, coherent, and
institutionally significant, but also structurally limited. Its regulatory perimeter is built
mainly around clubs, licence applicants, licensees, and licensors. This is
understandable, because clubs are the actors that manage the relevant financial flows,
incur sporting costs, pay wages, participate in transfers, receive UEFA revenues, and
may generate systemic financial risk. However, the credibility of football competitions
does not depend only on the financial sustainability of clubs. It also depends on the
independence, impartiality, and perceived integrity of match officials, designators,
video assistant referees, observers, and other actors involved in the administration of
the game.
The paper does not propose to extend the CFCB mechanically to referees. Referees are
not economic entities comparable to clubs, and they should not be subject to a general
financial control model designed for corporate football organizations. Instead, the paper
proposes a separate integrity and transparency framework for the refereeing sector,
inspired by some institutional features of the CFCB but adapted to a different purpose.
The proposed Referee Integrity and Transparency Body would be independent from
technical designation bodies and would focus on conflicts of interest, external
appointments, relations with clubs, agents and betting operators, gifts and hospitality,
whistleblowing, risk-based checks, audit of designations, and annual aggregate
reporting.
The central claim is that European football already has the institutional imagination to
build independent, procedural, evidence-based, and proportionate oversight
mechanisms. The next regulatory step should not be to replicate financial control
everywhere, but to develop differentiated oversight models for different sources of risk.
Club financial sustainability and referee integrity are distinct issues, but both are
essential to the credibility of modern football.

detail.abstract: The study evaluated the influence of capital structure over a ten (10) year period (between 2010 - 2019) in order to ascertain its effect on profitability for some selected subsets of SMEs in Ghana. Specifically, the research examined the effect the debt/equity ratio has on an SMEs profitability, the impact asset tangibility has on the productivity of these SMEs, the bearing of corporate tax on the productivity of the SMEs, and the consequence of the size of a business on the productivity of SMEs in Ghana. The methodology adopted for conducting this study was quantitative. Secondary data was used for the research. A sample of seven (7) SMEs in Ghana were sampled for the research. The multiple regression method was employed to ascertain the effects of the identified explanatory variables on the dependent variable. The results of the study revealed that the debt/equity ratio, asset tangibility, corporate tax, and business size were statistically important in predicting the profitability of the sampled SMEs in Ghana over the study period. The age of the SME (AGE) was the only insignificant predictor of profitability. The study recommends that all SMEs in Ghana should improve their overall information content to improve their capital structure decisions. Future research should consider the effects of risk management on the capital structure of SMEs in Ghana

detail.title: Labor-Oriented Management Control Mechanisms in the Modern Era
detail.abstract: This article provides an overview of two fundamental shifts in the modern workplace: the rise of hybrid and remote work, and the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI). I describe studies which examine hybrid or remote work and worker behavior, and highlight that management accounting scholars are uniquely placed to examine the effects of management controls in this context. Two papers in this Special Interest Forum do just that, while the third on the topic of hybrid/remote work examines how highlighting job characteristics affects job applications. While AI is not represented in this Forum, I highlight it as a fruitful area for management accounting research. Lastly, I emphasize that management accounting scholars should continue to advance more traditional research areas of labor-oriented management control mechanisms by leveraging new opportunities (e.g., regulation changes). The fourth paper in this Forum is illustrative of such research.

detail.abstract: On May 26, 2026, the DHS General Counsel issued a directive instructing ICE attorneys to pursue enforcement actions against immigration attorneys who file fraudulent asylum applications, invoking 8 U.S.C. § 1324c(d). This directive did not create new law. It enforced existing law: the same commitment to the integrity of the American immigration system codified in the Immigration Act of 1891, the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1952, and the Refugee Act of 1980. This paper argues that the directive responds to a structural failure: the systematic absence of professionals with direct and current institutional knowledge of the Venezuelan criminal justice system. That absence has enabled widespread document fraud — not because attorneys acted in bad faith, but because the tools to detect it never existed in the American market. The paper traces the historical foundations from Ellis Island to the present, quantifies the documented fiscal and human costs, and proposes a due diligence framework that meets the post-directive standard while honoring the American tradition of protecting those who genuinely deserve it.

detail.abstract: This paper studies dynamic choice under multi-prior ambiguity when the economic environment is open: probability mass can leave the active state space through regime-dependent structural ruin. The robust mean-variance-variance (M-V-V) criterion is attractive because it gives a tractable approximation to smooth ambiguity, but in dynamic portfolio problems it exhibits a horizon-scale inconsistency: ordinary path variance grows linearly in calendar time, while the ambiguity-variance penalty grows quadratically. This mismatch can overturn the usual monotonicity of risk aversion over long horizons. We show that the anomaly is a consequence of imposing M-V-V preferences on a closed, perpetual calendar-time geometry. The proposed Clock of Regimes (COR) framework replaces calendar time with Regime Time, the endogenous residence-time vector generated by the killed transition operator 𝐾 = 𝑄-𝐼 and the residence matrix 𝑁 = (-𝐾)-1. Under this nonconservative survival geometry, ambiguity penalties are localized by expected residence time rather than accumulated mechanically over the calendar horizon. The central result is a horizonrestoration theorem for admissible open survival networks. The COR representation bounds the quadratic horizon inflation and restores the monotone response of optimal risky allocations to risk aversion. We then characterize the associated dynamic stopping problem using a threeregime computation as a numerical illustration of the spectral mechanism.

title: The Economics of Marriage Payments: Bride Price, Dowry, and Dower
affiliations: University of British Columbia (UBC) - Vancouver School of Economics

detail.title: The Economics of Marriage Payments: Bride Price, Dowry, and Dower
detail.abstract:
Marriage payments are transfers made in connection with marriage and are among the most widespread and enduring institutions in human history. They can be categorized into three forms: bride price, paid by the groom or his family to the bride's parents; dowry, transferred from the bride's family to the groom or his kin; and dower, paid by the groom directly to the bride and retained as her property. Although their prevalence has declined in many industrialized societies, marriage payments remain common across large parts of Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Oceania.
Their persistence reflects the fact that they serve multiple economic and social functions simultaneously. Marriage payments can facilitate matching in marriage markets, redistribute marital surplus, transfer wealth across generations, provide insurance within marriage, and signal status, prestige, and adherence to social norms. 
Marriage payments influence a wide range of outcomes, including household savings, fertility decisions, child marriage, educational investments, migration, bargaining power within marriage, and marital stability. Their effects often extend beyond the married couple themselves, shaping intergenerational patterns of wealth transmission and human capital formation. 
As such, the consequences of marriage payments are far-reaching. Their welfare implications depend critically on the direction of transfers, who retains control over them after marriage, and the broader legal and social institutions in which they are embedded. In some settings, marital transfers can enhance women’s economic security and bargaining power. In others, they may contribute to gender inequality, violence, coercion, son preference, and constraints on women’s autonomy.
The significance of these welfare consequences warrants the attention of policymakers. Accordingly, marriage payments have generated considerable debate and ongoing efforts toward legal reform. At the same time, the diversity of marriage payment systems suggests caution in the design of public policy. Blanket prohibitions or externally imposed reforms may overlook the multiple functions these institutions perform and may generate unintended consequences. More promising approaches may focus on mitigating specific harmful features while preserving functions that families value, particularly where marriage payments remain deeply embedded in local social, economic, and legal systems.

title: Auditors' (Non-)Responses to Public Warnings of Audit Risk: Evidence from Short-Selling Campaigns
affiliations: Singapore Management University - School of Accountancy, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Harvard Business School and McGill University - Desautels Faculty of Management

detail.title: Auditors' (Non-)Responses to Public Warnings of Audit Risk: Evidence from Short-Selling Campaigns
detail.abstract: Using a novel setting, we examine auditors' responses to public warnings of audit risk and whether their non-responses are associated with auditor and client characteristics. Specifically, we focus on 243 short-selling campaigns from 2006 to 2020 in which short sellers make public, credible allegations of audit-related issues against listed companies. 48.3% of those companies' auditors do not take any observable actions in terms of raising audit fees substantially, terminating the engagement, issuing going concern opinions (GCO), or reporting internal control weaknesses (ICW) in the year after the short sellers' allegations. We further find that longer auditor-client tenure is the factor most consistently associated with auditors' non-response to public warnings of audit risk, a pattern arguably consistent with impaired independence. Additional analyses show that the litigation and reputation costs of auditors' inactions are minimal, further reducing auditors' incentives for responses.

title: Sui Generis Protection Of AI-Generated Outputs in Ukraine
affiliations: Intellectual Property Scientific Research Institute of the National Academy of Legal Sciences of Ukraine

detail.title: Sui Generis Protection Of AI-Generated Outputs in Ukraine
detail.abstract: The possibility and feasibility of legal protection for objects autonomously generated by AI technologies is a debatable issue. Some countries, notably the United Kingdom, offer copyright protection for such objects, while others do not recognize their copyrightability. There is also an example of the introduction of a special legal regime for autonomous computer creations, namely new sui generis right which came into force in Ukraine on January 1, 2023. This article reveals the main provisions of this regime and its positive features, such as a distinction between AIgenerated outputs and human works, non-recognition of the legal subjectivity of AI, and flexible determination of the right holders. At the same time, some aspects of the sui generis right to AIgenerated outputs raise concerns, particularly unclear criteria for the protectability, automatic granting of legal protection without any exceptions, a full range of exclusive rights, and a long duration of their validity. To avoid unjustified overprotection, the article suggests ways to improve the new regime by balancing the right to AI-generated outputs, considering the current state of technology development, and the interests of both potential rights holders and society.

title: Measuring Climate Change Adaptation: Are Countries Learning to Cope with Floods and Droughts?
affiliations: Decatab Pte Ltd

detail.title: Measuring Climate Change Adaptation: Are Countries Learning to Cope with Floods and Droughts?
detail.abstract:
Are countries adapting to climate-related disasters? This paper tests whether the
causal economic damage from floods and droughts is declining over time across 158
countries from 2000 to 2024—a direct, empirically grounded measure of adaptation
success. Standard panel regression approaches are ill-equipped to answer this question
because adaptive capacity—the institutional quality, infrastructure investment, and risk
culture that simultaneously affects both disaster probability and economic outcomes—is
an unobserved, time-varying confounder. Ignoring it biases estimated treatment effects
and compounds that bias when interacted with a time trend.
We address this challenge by extending the Time Series Deconfounder (Bica et al.,
2020), a causal machine learning framework that infers a substitute confounder from
the temporal structure of disaster assignments, bypassing the need to directly observe
adaptive capacity. Our extension introduces MC-dropout averaging for stable confounder
extraction in small panels and, critically, a within-country time-trend regression on
deconfounded individual treatment effects—a test with no analogue in the original
framework and our primary methodological contribution.
Using a 50-member GRU ensemble that averages over training stochasticity, we
find that both outcomes exhibit maladaptation over 2000–2024, though the pace is
decelerating sharply. For GDP per capita, the full-sample coefficient is ˆβGDP = −0.00051
(p < 0.001), indicating damage is growing by approximately 0.51% per decade on average. Maladaptation was most rapid in 2000–2009 ( ˆβ = −0.0020, approximately −0.20% per
year) and has since slowed to near-zero ( ˆβ = −0.00018, 2010–2024). For agricultural
value added, the full-sample coefficient is ˆβagri = −0.0194 percentage points per year
(p < 0.001), reflecting a catastrophic deterioration in 2000–2009 ( ˆβ = −0.085) that
has substantially decelerated in 2010–2024 ( ˆβ = +0.0018, near stabilisation). The only
income group showing GDP improvement is low-income countries ( ˆβ = +0.00032),
while high-income countries suffer the fastest-worsening GDP damage ( ˆβ = −0.00124).
Agricultural maladaptation is universal across all income groups and regions. Results are
robust to alternative treatment definitions, country-block bootstrap, and randomisation
inference.

title: Can Automation Offset Population Decline? Occupational Imbalances in a Shrinking Workforce
affiliations: and Bank of Korea

detail.title: Can Automation Offset Population Decline? Occupational Imbalances in a Shrinking Workforce
detail.abstract: This paper studies whether automation can mitigate the labor-market effects of population decline and how this mitigation differs across occupations. Korea's working-age population is projected to fall by about 11 percent between 2024 and 2034. Holding current occupational demand fixed, we first project occupation-level labor-supply imbalances using Korean population projections and age-by-occupation employment data. We then estimate occupation-level automation probabilities by applying a large language model (LLM) to O*NET task statements and mapping the resulting task-level measures to Korean occupations. Automation can substantially reduce the aggregate labor shortfall, but it does not eliminate occupational imbalance because automation potential is only weakly aligned with projected demographic shortages. The main implication is therefore compositional: population decline changes the distribution of labor scarcity, while automation changes where shortages persist and where surplus pressure emerges. With sufficiently rapid AI progress, the same framework implies that the policy problem may shift from aggregate labor shortage to the distribution of labor surplus across occupations.

title: Monetary Velocity in a Tokenized Economy: An Agent-Based Simulation of Liquidity Shocks and Programmable Friction
affiliations: JECRC University, Jaipur

detail.title: Monetary Velocity in a Tokenized Economy: An Agent-Based Simulation of Liquidity Shocks and Programmable Friction
detail.abstract: The transition toward real-world asset (RWA) tokenization represents a structural change in monetary dynamics by transforming previously illiquid capital into liquid, spendable assets. This study employs an agent-based model to examine how such liquidity shocks affect the velocity of money in a closed economy over a 100-day horizon. Three institutional settings are compared: a traditional economy with illiquid assets, an unregulated tokenized market, and a regulated tokenized system with a 30% programmable transaction friction. Within the simulated environment, unregulated tokenization increases the velocity index by approximately 11.19% and amplifies daily volatility. Introducing programmable friction reduces velocity by about 2.22% relative to the unregulated case while maintaining circulation above the traditional baseline. The findings suggest that embedded regulatory mechanisms can moderate liquidity-driven volatility while preserving key benefits of tokenization.

title: Individual Sovereignty and Other-Regarding Preferences

detail.title: Individual Sovereignty and Other-Regarding Preferences
detail.abstract: We consider the social aggregation of preferences over lotteries in the presence of other-regarding preferences. If society respects each individual's sovereignty, an axiom we propose akin to Sen's Liberalism, then society's utility is a linear combination of individuals' self-regarding utilities. That is, other-regarding preferences can only influence the weights society places on each individual. We next characterize the unique weighting method under which society's weight ratio between two individuals is the geometric mean of that of all individuals. The first distinguishing axiom concerns the consistency of sequential aggregation, while the second concerns consensus across changes in individuals' other-regarding preferences. We extend these results to a setting with feasibility constraints and a setting with subjective uncertainty.

title: Coalition Stability with Complementary Goods
affiliations: Drexel University and Agricultural University of Athens

detail.title: Coalition Stability with Complementary Goods
detail.abstract: We study coalition stability in markets with differentiated complementary goods. Coordination among complementors internalizes positive demand spillovers and expands output, but also creates incentives for outsider free riding and insider defection. We analyze a quantity-competition model in which a subset of firms coordinates quantities while remaining firms act independently. Full coordination can be stable in small markets but becomes difficult to sustain as the number of firms grows. When full coordination is unstable, stable partial coalitions always exist and, unlike in standard substitute-goods environments, can involve more than two firms. In very large markets, stable coalition size remains bounded, implying that coordination does not scale with market size. We also show that participation-contingent governance mechanisms, such as compatibility standards, APIs, and bundling arrangements, can stabilize otherwise unstable coordination by making coordination rents partially excludable. The results characterize how complementarity fundamentally changes coalition stability incentives relative to substitute-goods markets and provide a theory of self-enforcing coordination among complementors.

title: Helpful Bounceback: Definition, Typology, and Diagnosis of Execution Avoidance in LLM-Based AI Systems

detail.abstract:
Large language model (LLM) based AI systems exhibit a recurrent failure mode in which they convert executable tasks into natural-language guidance directed at the user, despite possessing the capability to execute those tasks via available tools, code-execution environments, or function-calling interfaces. We name this pattern Helpful Bounceback (HB) — in Korean, 친절한 떠넘기기 — and argue, on conceptual rather than empirical grounds, that it constitutes a behavioral category not reducible to sycophancy, sandbagging, overrefusal, or the informal notion of "laziness," though it intersects with each.

The paper advances four contributions. First, an operational definition built on four jointly necessary and jointly sufficient elements: a capability–action gap, non-execution, a modality shift from execution to explanation, and burden transfer to the user. Second, a three-layer causal account on which HB emerges only when RLHF-induced verbosity bias, safety-training overgeneralization, and Goodhart-type specification gaming co-occur. Third, an empirical typology of five HB manifestations — instructive substitution, placeholder insertion, tool avoidance, premature termination, and shallow execution — anchored in peer-reviewed and clearly demarcated gray-literature sources. Fourth, a four-dimensional diagnostic framework with a five-step operationalization roadmap and five falsifiable predictions.

The contribution is conceptual, not empirical: no new primary data are presented, and the framework is offered as a definitional scaffold against which empirical work — including the preregistered protocol of the companion paper — can proceed against a fixed analytic target. This is the first paper in a two-paper companion series; the companion paper (Kim, 2026b) develops the Execution Authority Protocol, a user-side mitigation methodology. Earlier versions of this paper through v2.1 used the term Performative Helpfulness.

title: A Riemann Wald Couple
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: A Riemann Wald Couple
detail.abstract: We give a probabilistic reformulation of the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) in which the non-trivial zeros appear twice: as the characteristic zeros of Pólya's symmetric law X ξ (characteristic function Ξ(t)/Ξ(0)), and as the exponential rates of its van Dantzig/Wald dual H ξ. The dual is a generalized gamma convolution (GGC); on the critical line it is the explicit infinite convolution H ξ = γρ>0 Exp(rate γ 2 ρ), U 1/2 = γρ>0 δ γ 2 ρ , the Thorin measure being the counting measure on the squared ordinates. Two analytic ingredients organise the construction. Polson's Gamma(2) scale mixture makes the primal kernel infinitely divisible (Kristiansen), and the 2 sin 2 lemma, which makes-log ζ(σ + it)/ζ(σ) negative-definite for σ > 1 via the kernel 2 sin 2 (tx/2) against the von Mangoldt measure, exhibits the relevant positivity unconditionally for σ > 1. These act on the primal side; the dual's Lévy density κ satisfies U = L-1 [κ], and the dual is a GGC, equivalently κ completely monotone, equivalently the signed measure U Polson recovers by Stieltjes inversion is positive, if and only if RH. We are careful to note that this dual condition admits no weaker unconditional floor: on the dual side, infinite divisibility, GGC and RH coincide, and the primal ID floor does not reduce it. Riemann's incomplete-gamma representation, an everywhere-convergent form, carries the construction into the strip 1 2 < σ < 1. A numerical audit confirms the governing identity to five significant figures over λ ∈ (0, 100) and resolves U into peaks at γ 2 ρ. We keep a two-tier discipline throughout, construction unconditional, positivity of U RH-equivalent. The reformulation is an equivalence, not a proof.

title: A Riemann Thorin-van Dantzig principle
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: A Riemann Thorin-van Dantzig principle
detail.abstract: Two probabilistic programmes attack the location of zeros of an even entire function: the van Dantzig-Lukacs programme, which asks whether the function lies in the Laguerre-Pólya class D L , and the Thorin-Bondesson programme, which studies the reciprocal as the Laplace transform of a generalised gamma convolution (GGC) and reads the zeros off the Thorin measure. We prove a transfer principle that makes the two programmes a single object. Concretely, to a Laplace exponent Ψ of a spectrally negative Lévy process we attach a van Dantzig function J Ψ , a self-decomposable subordinator T Ψ and a symmetric variable D Ψ = √ 2 B TΨ ; we show that T Ψ is a GGC precisely on the Thorin-Bernstein sub-cone TBF of the Bernstein cone that already carries Ψ, that on this sub-cone the van Dantzig pair [J Ψ , 1/I Ψ ] is exactly a Wald couple, and that J Ψ ∈ D L iff the Thorin measure is supported on (0, ∞) and carried by the squared zeros. The engine is a corrected sine-squared transform that produces the Thorin density in closed form from a Lévy representation; because the kernel is a square, positivity of the Thorin density is automatic when the Lévy measure is positive. For ξ the relevant measure is signed (the archimedean part negative, the prime part positive), so positivity is not automatic but a cancellation, which is exactly where the Riemann hypothesis sits. Applied to the Riemann ξ-function this yields a clean two-tier statement: an unconditional GGC representation of the reciprocal for every base point α > 1, and a conditional reduction of the Riemann hypothesis to the survival of that representation at the critical base point α = 1 2. We compute each zero's contribution to the Thorin measure in closed form (a Lorentzian profile that collapses to an atom at the squared ordinate) and track the residual fractional drift left by the genus-one factors, so that a zero-free half-plane to the right of α is necessary for the reciprocal to be a generalised gamma convolution, and the Riemann hypothesis is the equivalence at α = 1 2. We then isolate the single positivity statement that bears the weight, relate it to the de Bruijn-Newman flow (which moves the Thorin measure, while the Gaussian drift of the symmetric GGC provably cannot move the zeros), and unify the Lukacs and Bondesson closure calculi.

title: Societal Conditions for Electoral Implementation of a Planner's Policy
affiliations: University of Granada

detail.title: Societal Conditions for Electoral Implementation of a Planner's Policy
detail.abstract: This paper studies when the policy preferred by a benevolent planner can be implemented through electoral competition. We consider a two-candidate setting in which candidates simultaneously announce policies, voters vote sincerely under majority rule, and the winning candidate implements her announced policy. We show that two conditions are necessary and sufficient for the planner's policy to arise as the unique pure-strategy Nash equilibrium policy outcome. Collective stability requires voters to be sufficiently aligned with the planner's policy, so that relevant deviations are defeated under majority voting. Candidate differentiation requires sufficient divergence in candidates' preferences to rule out alternative common announcements that could also be sustained in equilibrium. The analysis shows how the internal configuration of society, understood as the joint structure of voters' and candidates' preferences, can determine whether a target policy is politically implementable without institutional change.

title: The Economic Impact of Unauthorised Immigration: A Critical Cross-National Analysis of Fiscal, Labour Market, and Macroeconomic Dimensions

detail.title: The Economic Impact of Unauthorised Immigration: A Critical Cross-National Analysis of Fiscal, Labour Market, and Macroeconomic Dimensions
detail.abstract: This paper critically evaluates the economic effects of unauthorised immigration on host economies through a cross-national comparative lens, drawing on empirical evidence published between 2020 and 2026. The analysis examines twelve major host economies across four continents: the European Union (with detailed evidence from Germany, Italy, Spain, France, and Poland), the United Kingdom, the Russian Federation, Türkiye, the Gulf Cooperation Council states, South Africa, Malaysia, Thailand, India, Brazil, the United States, and Canada. Five questions structure the inquiry: the global magnitude and distribution of unauthorised migrant populations; fiscal contributions and costs across diverse institutional contexts; labour market impacts on native workers; sectoral concentrations; and macroeconomic effects, including projected consequences of large-scale removal. Synthesis of authoritative sources indicates that approximately 5.8 million unauthorised migrants reside in EU-27 member states, 2.9 million in the Russian Federation, 2.2 million in South Africa, 2.7 million in Malaysia, 2.4 million in Thailand, and 3.6 million Syrians remain under Temporary Protection in Türkiye (International Organization for Migration [IOM], 2025; Eurostat, 2025; United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees [UNHCR], 2025). The Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD, 2025) estimates that the 2019-2024 immigration surge raised hostcountry potential gross domestic product (GDP) by an average of 1.4 percent across destination economies. The International Monetary Fund (Allen et al., 2024) projects that mass-removal scenarios in major host economies would reduce GDP by 1.8-6.2 percent over five years, with disproportionate impacts in agriculture, construction, and care sectors. Türkiye Statistical Institute (TÜİK, 2024) data indicate that Syrian-owned enterprises generated approximately US$2.3 billion in annual turnover by 2023. The paper argues that aggregate net economic benefits coexist with genuinely localised fiscal costs and distributional pressures on competing low-skill workers, and that policy responses should be calibrated accordingly. Recommendations include regularisation pathways, intensified employer-side labour-standards enforcement, targeted fiscal transfers to high-impact localities, and sectoral guest-worker reforms.

title: Hybrid Expectations, Financial Frictions, and Macroeconomic Dynamics in a Small Open Economy within a Monetary Union
affiliations: and University of Ljubljana - Faculty of Economics

detail.title: Hybrid Expectations, Financial Frictions, and Macroeconomic Dynamics in a Small Open Economy within a Monetary Union
detail.abstract: This paper estimates a DSGE model with financial frictions and hybrid expectations, a novelty in modelling small open economy within a monetary union. We find that both features improve the in-sample fit. Forecast error variance decompositions indicate that dampening the endogenous mechanics of financial frictions shifts the influence of financial shocks on real loans to non-financial corporations, real investments, and domestic nominal interest rates toward demand and foreign shocks. Adding hybrid expectations, in turn, amplifies the effects of demand and supply shocks across most observed variables, while diminishing the role of foreign and financial shocks. Analysis of impulse response functions suggests that hybrid expectations have a greater impact on the persistence and magnitudes of economic responses than the endogenous mechanics of financial frictions. Despite superior in-sample fit, hybrid expectations do not enhance forecasting accuracy over an eight-quarters ahead horizon, particularly for real GDP. Moreover, financial frictions offer somewhat modest forecasting gains, contributing to ongoing debates about their value during periods of financial stability.

title: Execution Authority Protocol: User-Side Mitigation of Helpful Bounceback via Meta-Prompting

detail.title: Execution Authority Protocol: User-Side Mitigation of Helpful Bounceback via Meta-Prompting

detail.abstract:
This is the second paper in a two-paper companion series. The first paper (Kim, 2026a) operationally defines Helpful Bounceback (HB) — in Korean, 친절한 떠넘기기 — as a behavioral pattern in which large language models, despite possessing task-relevant capabilities, shift from execution to explanation and transfer cognitive burden to users, supplying a three-layer causal account, a five-category typology, and a four-dimensional diagnostic, but deliberately stopping short of intervention. The present paper closes the diagnosis–intervention gap by proposing the Execution Authority Protocol (EAP), a user-side meta-prompting methodology that targets each of the three causal layers without modifying model weights.

EAP comprises five principles — Identity Reframing, Explicit Authority Delegation, Preemptive Modality Locking, Anti-Bounceback Constraint, and Escalation Protocol — operationalized through a five-block implementation template (Identity, Authority, Behavioral Modality, Workflow, Output Format), grounded in prior empirical findings on role-based prompting, meta-prompting for AI systems, and reason–act loops.

The paper advances four contributions: (i) a theoretical account of why user-side meta-prompting can attenuate HB despite training-induced biases, developed through four theoretical commitments (anti-monocausality, compositionality, layer-independence of counter-levers, architectural analogy with weight-level alignment); (ii) the first systematization of EAP as a named methodology with five independently falsifiable principles, each under a uniform six-part structure; (iii) an implementation-ready template with context-specific strategies for code generation, data analysis, multi-tool (MCP), and long-horizon agentic settings; and (iv) a preregistrable evaluation protocol using paired prompts in a leave-one-principle-out factorial, the Kim (2026a) diagnostic, pre-specified Holm–Bonferroni correction, and sensitivity analysis across four effect-size scenarios.

The paper is methodological, not empirical: the Section 7 protocol is a design specification, not a completed study; empirical claims should be read as predictions rather than findings. Principle 4 was formerly named the Anti-Performative-Helpfulness Constraint, and the phenomenon was formerly named Performative Helpfulness (companion paper through v2.1).

title: Profits, Power and the Tariff Revival: A Kalecki-Hirschman Interpretation of Contemporary U.S. Trade Policy
affiliations: Athens University of Economics and Business

detail.title: Profits, Power and the Tariff Revival: A Kalecki-Hirschman Interpretation of Contemporary U.S. Trade Policy
detail.abstract: The resurgence of tariffs as a central instrument of U.S. economic policy represents one of the most consequential departures from the liberal trade consensus of the post-Cold War era. This article examines that evolution through the combined lenses of Kalecki's theory of aggregate profits and Hirschman's theory of asymmetric trade dependence. It argues that these two frameworks illuminate complementary dimensions of the contemporary tariff regime: Kalecki's macroeconomic identity identifies the structural channels through which import compression and investment inducement may influence the aggregate mass of profits, whilst Hirschman's analysis reveals how trade restrictions can reconfigure patterns of dependence and generate opportunities for political leverage. Together they suggest that tariffs possess a structural attractivenesscompatible simultaneously with profit maintenance and geopolitical influencethat helps explain their durability across administrations with quite different priorities. The argument is offered as a theoretical and interpretive contribution, not as a causal hypothesis to be tested. It does not displace existing explanations centred on strategic rivalry, industrial policy, or domestic coalitions, but proposes that the interaction between accumulation and asymmetric dependence represents an underappreciated dimension of the contemporary political economy of trade. More broadly, the article contributes to ongoing debates concerning the relationship between accumulation, state power, and the changing governance of international economic relations.

title: Pál Szilágyi: The Human Factor in EU Competition Law: The Liability of Non-Human Companies for Antitrust Infringements – A Quick Take
affiliations: Competition Law Research Centre

detail.title: Pál Szilágyi: The Human Factor in EU Competition Law: The Liability of Non-Human Companies for Antitrust Infringements – A Quick Take
detail.abstract: In June 2026, the Argentine government proposed a new corporate category — the non-human corporation — operated by AI agents or robots, endowed with limited liability, with human shareholders optional. Conceived as a deregulatory device for walling risk inside an autonomous entity, it poses a question EU competition law has not yet confronted: can such an entity be held liable for an antitrust infringement, and if so, who pays? This paper argues that the answer turns on the functional concept of the undertaking rather than on corporate form. Because Article 101 TFEU looks past legal status and national registration, a non-human corporation offering goods or services on a market is an undertaking like any other, and its Argentine pedigree affords no immunity — least of all given the extraterritorial reach of EU competition law. The decisive questions are ones of attribution. Where a human or corporate parent controls the entity, the Akzo presumption of decisive influence pierces the limited-liability wall and exposes the controllers. Where the entity is genuinely ownerless and run by non-deterministic autonomous agents, the paper identifies a real but bounded enforcement gap: true algorithmic autonomy may negate the concurrence of wills that Article 101 requires (the conscious-parallelism limit of Wood Pulp), while non-determinism defeats the human-awareness pivot on which attribution doctrines such as Eturas rest. Liability, if it attaches at all, then falls on a thinly capitalised and likely judgment-proof entity. EU competition law thus remains applicable to non-human corporations in principle; what strains is its anthropocentric attribution architecture — designed for human cartelists — at precisely the point where autonomy and ownerlessness coincide.

title: Generative Predictive Distributions for Time Series
affiliations: and University of Helsinki - Department of Political and Economic Studies

detail.title: Generative Predictive Distributions for Time Series
detail.abstract: We propose a flexible framework for modeling the predictive distributions of nonlinear, possibly multivariate time series. Our approach expresses a general predictive distribution in an appropriate generative representation that is based on a folklore result from measure theoretic probability. This representation provides a direct simulation-based approximation to the predictive distribution, enabling straightforward computation of forecasts for the conditional mean and variance, fan charts, value at risk, expected shortfall, joint tail risks, and other quantities of interest. We estimate this generative representation using a version of conditional generative adversarial networks and provide a formal statistical analysis of estimation under weak temporal dependence. Specifically, estimation is expressed as a particular minimax problem and we establish consistency of its approximate solutions in Hausdorff distance. The empirical relevance of the approach is illustrated using applications to equity returns, realized variance, and realized covariances. The proposed method is also computationally manageable, with estimation in our applications taking approximately one minute on a standard laptop.

title: A Thorin Approach to Computing Primes
affiliations: University of Chicago - Booth School of Business

detail.title: A Thorin Approach to Computing Primes
detail.abstract: We develop two complementary Thorin representations of the Riemann zeta function. The first, grounded in the Euler product for real s > 1, identifies log ζ(s) = ∞ 0 e-su dΛ(u) where Λ = p,k k-1 δ k log p is the von Mangoldt measure. This is a Laplace transform on the real axis, completely monotone and unconditional. The second, following Polson (2021), represents ξ(1 2)/ξ(1 2 + √ s) as the Laplace transform of a G subordinator with Thorin measure U ξ = τ δ τ 2 supported on the squared imaginary parts of the non-trivial zeros. We clarify the computational and structural content of each. On the computational side, analytic inversion of U ξ reduces to zero-finding for ξ and is exponentially ill-conditioned (κ ∼ e cN) due to the clustering of squared zeros τ 2 n ; numerical experiments confirm breakdown at N ≈ 10-12 in double precision. On the structural side, the Thorin framework provides a genuine dictionary: RH is equivalent to U ξ being a non-negative measure; simple zeros correspond to pure exponential convolution; the functional equation encodes Wald-couple symmetry; and de Bruijn-Newman flow is a one-parameter deformation of U ξ. For computational recovery of π(x), the von Mangoldt Thorin representation via Post-Widder inversion and Generative Bayesian Computation (GBC) is the correct unconditional route, making no appeal to the Riemann Hypothesis or complex arithmetic.

title: Land, Power and Population Density in the Global Population Shifts of 1500 -1960
affiliations: ,  and Brown University

detail.title: Land, Power and Population Density in the Global Population Shifts of 1500 -1960
detail.abstract: The regional distribution of world population underwent profound changes during the age of exploration and colonization, in which a handful of European powers colonized the better part of the remaining continents. One consequence is that countries in the Americas, Australia and New Zealand, after sharp contractions of indigenous populations following exposure to Old World diseases, today have populations in which European or African descendants form majorities and speak predominantly European languages. Migration and in some cases colonization also altered population compositions in countries including South Africa, Cape Verde, Fiji and Singapore. And descendants of émigrés came to outnumber those of "stayers" in some non-colonizing countries, including Ireland and Lebanon. We identify major determinants of who settled where, during this era of colonialism and migration, demonstrating that both "natural" factors like availability and fertility of agricultural land and climate and disease prevalence, on the one hand, and power inequalities and cultural variables, on the other, explain the broad patterns of migration.

title: An Adaptive Piano-Inspired Memristive Fractional-Order Cryptosystem for Secure Image Protection

detail.title: An Adaptive Piano-Inspired Memristive Fractional-Order Cryptosystem for Secure Image Protection
detail.abstract: The growing need for secure image transmission across public networks requires robust encryption algorithms. Traditional chaos-based image ciphers typically have a small key space, weak avalanche behavior, or are susceptible to differential cryptanalysis. To overcome such inadequacies, this paper suggests a new adaptive image cryptosystem that combines a fractional-order memristive chaotic engine and a non-linear hybrid encryption kernel. The system uses piano-inspired feedback; the keystream generator dynamically adapts to the previously encrypted pixel, enabling powerful Cipher Block Chaining (CBC)- style chaining and content-dependent diffusion. A four-dimensional memristive system is solved by the use of fractional-order calculus, which gives an ultra-large key space (>1080) and very high sensitivity to initial conditions—confirmed by a positive largest Lyapunov exponent (1.7199). The encryption kernel maps the traditional Exclusive OR (XOR) with the reversible two-step operation: the modular addition of the plaintext with the first keystream byte and the XOR with the second keystream one, both of which increase non-linearity and confusion. Large-scale experiments with six standard 256 × 256 colour images indicate almost ideal entropy (7.9994), Number of Pixel Change Rate (NPCR) which is 99.62, Unified Average Changing Intensity (UACI) which is 33.43, correlation coefficients are near to zero, very low Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) homogeneity (≈0.017) and high contrast (≈4843) and low energy (≈0.006 The ciphertext passes seven National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) SP-800-22 statistical tests, is extremely sensitive to keys (a perturbation of 1 × 10−14 alters >99.6% of ciphertext) and resists chosen-plaintext and known-plaintext attacks. Decryption has linear time complexity O(N), and average encryption and decryption times are 3.40 s and 2.75 s for 256 × 256 images. The proposed cryptosystem provides an attractive security–performance trade-off that can be used in high-security systems like medical image protection, privacy-preserving multimedia transmission, and secure cloud storage.
